requirement: Engine models 8 input strips (5 hardware, 3 virtual) routable to any of 8 output buses (A1-A5 physical, B1-B3 virtual) via independent on/off routing bits per strip-bus pair.
acceptance_test: Unit test asserts a 8x8 boolean routing table exists and any strip can be independently enabled/disabled to any bus without affecting others.

requirement: Each of the 5 physical (hardware) strips carries exactly 2 audio channels internally.
acceptance_test: Property test: physical strip buffer width is fixed at 2 channels regardless of device format negotiated.

requirement: Each of the 3 virtual strips (VIO, AUX, VIO3) carries 8 audio channels internally (7.1 layout: L,R,C,LFE,SL,SR,BL,BR).
acceptance_test: Property test: virtual strip buffers are fixed at 8 channels; channel order matches L,R,C,LFE,SL,SR,BL,BR.

feature: Total input/output channel count (34 in / 64 out)
requirement: Engine exposes 34 total input channels (5x2 + 3x8) and 64 total output channels (8 buses x 8 channels) for insert/callback purposes.
acceptance_test: Unit test sums per-strip and per-bus channel widths and asserts totals of 34 and 64.

requirement: Every one of the 8 buses (A1-A5, B1-B3) is internally 8 channels wide regardless of the physical device's channel count, to support 5.1/7.1.
acceptance_test: Unit test: a bus configured with a 2-channel physical device still processes and exposes 8 internal channels.

requirement: The real-time audio callback path performs no heap allocation and no locking; parameter changes reach the audio thread via lock-free SPSC/MPSC queues.
acceptance_test: Integration test runs the audio callback under a allocation-tracking/lock-tracking harness (e.g. custom global allocator + loom/miri-style checks) for 10k callback cycles while parameters are being changed concurrently and asserts zero allocations and zero blocking calls.
notes: Core non-functional architecture requirement from decision spine.

requirement: When the control thread pushes parameter changes faster than the audio thread drains them, the queue must not block the audio thread and must not lose the most recent value for a given parameter.
acceptance_test: Property test floods the queue with rapid updates to the same parameter and asserts the audio thread eventually observes the last-written value with no panics or drops of unrelated parameters.

requirement: When a device is selected on bus A1, its sample rate becomes the engine's master sample rate for all DSP processing and for the virtual ASIO drivers' configuration.
acceptance_test: Integration test selects an A1 backend at 48000 Hz and asserts the engine's internal processing rate and virtual-ASIO negotiated rate are both 48000 Hz.

feature: Internal clock fallback when no A1 device
requirement: If no device is selected on bus A1, the engine runs on an internal master clock at the user's Preferred Main Sample Rate and a configurable Buffering Clock size, so the mixer keeps operating headless.
acceptance_test: Integration test: with no A1 backend attached, engine starts, advances the internal clock, and processes buffers at the configured Preferred Main Sample Rate / Buffering Clock size.

requirement: Preferred Main Sample Rate accepts 32000, 44100, 48000, 88200, 96000, 176400, 192000 Hz.
acceptance_test: Property test iterates the 7 documented rates and confirms each is accepted by Option.sr and rejects an out-of-list value.

feature: Automatic sample-rate conversion to master rate
requirement: Any input or output point running at a sample rate different from the engine master rate is transparently sample-rate-converted to/from the master rate.
acceptance_test: Integration test feeds a synthetic input device at 44100 Hz into an engine running at 48000 Hz and asserts output pitch/duration match a golden reference within tolerance (no audible artifact threshold, e.g. THD+N below X dB).

feature: Buffer size ranges per backend class
requirement: Buffering is configurable per backend class: MME 512-2048 samples (default 1024), WDM/KS 128-2048 (documented default 512, floor down to 256 in UI), ASIO 128-2048 or driver default (0).
acceptance_test: Property test validates each backend's buffer-size setter clamps/rejects values outside its documented range and accepts the documented default.

requirement: Engine surfaces a stability warning/telemetry event when a backend buffer is configured below 256 samples at 44.1/48 kHz, matching the vendor's documented stability caveat.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets buffer size to 128 and asserts a stability-risk flag/event is emitted.

requirement: A null/loopback host-I/O backend exists behind the same trait as WASAPI/CoreAudio/PipeWire, producing/consuming silence or looped-back audio deterministically so 100% of engine tests run on Linux CI without real hardware.
acceptance_test: CI integration test suite runs the entire engine test matrix using only the null backend on a Linux runner and reports pass with zero real-device dependencies.

feature: One trait for all host-I/O backends
requirement: WASAPI/KS/ASIO (Windows), CoreAudio (macOS), and PipeWire/ALSA (Linux) host-I/O implementations conform to one shared Rust trait for device enumeration, open/close, and buffer callback.
acceptance_test: Unit test compiles a mock backend against the trait and asserts the trait's required methods are implemented; integration test swaps backends behind a feature flag with no engine-code changes.

requirement: Windows kernel driver, macOS HAL plug-in, and PipeWire virtual nodes implement one shared virtual-device trait for exposing engine strips/buses as OS-level playback/recording endpoints.
acceptance_test: Unit test compiles a mock virtual-device backend against the trait; integration test on the null backend exercises create/destroy of a virtual endpoint.

requirement: A pre-fader insert callback point exposes all 34 input channels (and 34 outputs) to an external processing client, selectable PRE-FX (default) or POST-FX per Patch.PostFxInsert.
acceptance_test: Integration test registers a mock insert client, verifies it receives exactly 34 input channels in the documented per-strip order and its output is summed back before the fader stage when PRE, after strip FX when POST.

requirement: An output insert callback (pre-master, 64 buffers) and a main callback (all inputs after input insert + all outputs after master gain) are available to registered clients.
acceptance_test: Integration test registers callbacks at each of the three documented points and asserts each fires with the correct channel count and at the documented stage of the signal path.

spec_ref: Decision spine + PM p.66-70 script grammar
requirement: All strip/bus/fx/patch/option/recorder parameters are represented as a single authoritative state store that both the control API and internal engine consumers read, so RT-packet, GUI, and script layers stay consistent.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets a parameter via the control API and asserts it is observable identically via a get-parameter call and via the RT/telemetry snapshot within one processing block.

requirement: Strip[i].Mute is a 0/1 boolean that silences the strip's contribution to all buses.
acceptance_test: Unit test mutes a strip and asserts zero output energy on every bus fed by that strip.

requirement: Strip[i].Solo is 0/1; when any strip is soloed, all non-soloed strips are effectively muted from the mix.
acceptance_test: Unit test solos strip N and asserts only strip N's signal reaches the output while other strips are silent.

requirement: Strip[i].Mono is 0/1 and merges channel 1 and 2 into an identical mono signal on both channels for hardware strips only.
acceptance_test: Unit test feeds distinct L/R test tones, enables Mono, and asserts both output channels are bit-identical (sum of L+R per documented behavior).

requirement: Strip[i].MC (0/1) mutes channel 3 (center) of a virtual strip's 8-channel signal, used to remove dialog from 5.1/7.1 sources.
acceptance_test: Unit test enables MC on a virtual strip with signal on all 8 channels and asserts channel 3 is silenced while channels 1,2,4-8 pass through.

requirement: Strip[i].Gain accepts -60 dB to +12 dB, default 0 dB.
acceptance_test: Property test sets Gain across the full range in 0.1 dB steps and asserts measured output level matches target within tolerance; out-of-range values are clamped or rejected.

requirement: Strip[i].GainLayer[j] (j=0..7) provides an independent -60..+12 dB gain per strip per bus, active only in the Max feature set.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets different GainLayer values for the same strip on two different buses and asserts each bus receives the strip at its own independent gain.

requirement: Option.SliderMode selects whether moving a strip's main fader sets every bus gain-layer to the same value (ABSOLUTE, default) or shifts all gain-layers by the same delta, preserving their relative differences (RELATIVE).
acceptance_test: Unit test sets distinct gain-layer values per bus, moves the main fader in RELATIVE mode, and asserts each layer's original offset from the others is preserved; repeats in ABSOLUTE mode and asserts all layers converge to the same value.

requirement: Strip[i].FadeTo=(dBTarget, msTime) ramps the strip gain to dBTarget over msTime milliseconds (0-120000 ms).
acceptance_test: Unit test issues FadeTo(-20, 1000) from 0 dB and samples gain at t=0, t=500ms, t=1000ms, asserting a monotonic ramp reaching -20 dB at completion within tolerance.

requirement: Strip[i].FadeBy=(dBDelta, msTime) ramps the strip gain by a relative dB delta over msTime milliseconds.
acceptance_test: Unit test issues FadeBy(+6, 500) from an arbitrary starting gain and asserts the final gain equals start+6 dB after 500ms.

feature: Limit remote gain to 0 dB option
requirement: A global option caps MIDI/remote-driven gain moves at 0 dB instead of +12 dB when enabled, without limiting mouse-driven moves.
acceptance_test: Unit test enables the option, issues a remote relative gain increase past 0 dB, and asserts the resulting gain is clamped at 0 dB.

requirement: Strip[i].Pan_x/Pan_y (-0.5..+0.5 / 0..1.0), Color_x/Color_y (-0.5..+0.5 / 0..1.0), fx_x/fx_y (-0.5..+0.5 / 0..1.0) each address a distinct 2D panel (binaural position, tonal color EQ, chorus/phaser modulation) on hardware strips only.
acceptance_test: Property test sweeps each x/y pair across its documented range and asserts the corresponding DSP effect (pan position, EQ curve, modulation depth) responds monotonically and virtual strips reject/ignore the physical-only parameters.

requirement: Strip[i].Pan_x/Pan_y on virtual strips place the source among 5 speaker positions (FL, FC, FR, RL, RR) via the same -0.5..0.5 coordinate space.
acceptance_test: Unit test places the pan pot at documented corner positions and asserts energy is routed to the corresponding channel(s) only.

requirement: A single 0-10 knob drives a combined compressor/gate effect, retained as the baseline dynamics control for simple strips.
acceptance_test: Golden test compares output loudness/gate behavior at knob values 0, 5, 10 against reference curves.

requirement: Strip[i].Comp (0-10) drives a compressor with automatic make-up gain, boosting perceived loudness as the knob increases.
acceptance_test: Golden test measures gain reduction and output RMS across knob values 0..10 against a reference compressor curve.

requirement: Strip[i].Comp.GainIn (-24..+24 dB), .Ratio (1..8), .Threshold (-40..-3 dB), .Attack (0..200 ms), .Release (0..5000 ms), .Knee (0..1), .GainOut (-24..+24 dB), .MakeUp (0/1) fully parameterize the compressor.
acceptance_test: Property test sets each detailed parameter to its min/max/mid and asserts the compressor transfer function (threshold, ratio, knee shape) matches a reference DSP model within tolerance; MakeUp=1 auto-computes GainOut.

requirement: Moving the simple Comp knob after detailed parameters were edited re-derives all detailed parameters from the knob's default curve (PRG behavior); an undo restores the prior detailed values.
acceptance_test: Unit test edits detail params, moves the knob, asserts detail params reset to the knob-default curve, then invokes undo and asserts the prior detail values are restored.

requirement: Strip[i].Gate (0-10) drives a noise gate effect.
acceptance_test: Golden test measures gate open/close behavior across knob values against a reference curve.

requirement: Strip[i].Gate.Threshold (-60..-10 dB), .Damping (-60..-10 dB, default off/-inf), .BPSidechain (100..4000 Hz, default off), .Attack (0..1000 ms), .Hold (0..5000 ms), .Release (0..5000 ms) fully parameterize the gate, including an optional band-pass sidechain.
acceptance_test: Property test sets each parameter to documented bounds and asserts gate open/close timing and sidechain filtering match a reference model.

requirement: Strip[i].Denoiser (0-10) and Strip[i].Denoiser.Threshold (0-10, 'Noise Floor Remover') reduce/remove noise floor; a non-zero setting adds processing latency to the strip.
acceptance_test: Golden test measures noise-floor reduction in dB across knob settings against a reference noise-reduction curve; latency test asserts reported strip latency increases only when Denoiser>0.

requirement: Strip[i].Denoiser.Bypass (0/1) disables denoiser processing while preserving its stored settings.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets Bypass=1 and asserts the signal passes unmodified even with Denoiser>0.

requirement: Strip[i].Pitch.On (0/1), .DryWet (-100..+100%), .PitchValue (-12..+12 semitones), .LoFormant/.MedFormant/.HiFormant (-12..+12 each) implement a real-time pitch/formant shifter with dry/wet blend.
acceptance_test: Golden test pitch-shifts a reference tone by +12 and -12 semitones and asserts detected pitch matches target within cents tolerance; formant sweep asserts spectral envelope shift.

requirement: Strip[i].Pitch.RecallPreset (0-7, write-only) recalls one of 8 factory Voice Modeler presets (documented UI labels P-3/P+3/P-6/P+6/P-9/P+9/P-12/P+12).
acceptance_test: Unit test recalls each of the 8 presets and asserts the resulting Pitch.* parameter set matches the documented preset table.

requirement: Strip[i].Karaoke (0-4) selects OFF or one of four algorithms: K-m (stereo common-part/voice removal), K-1 (keep some bass/treble), K-2 (keep more bass/treble), Kv (200-4000 Hz band-reject voice filter on mono-compatible material).
acceptance_test: Golden test runs each of the 4 algorithms against a reference stereo vocal+instrumental mix and asserts vocal energy is reduced per algorithm's documented behavior; OFF passes signal unmodified.

requirement: Strip[i].Limit (-40..+12 dB) applies a brick-wall/soft limiter before the gain slider on Plus/Max-tier strips (both physical and virtual).
acceptance_test: Property test drives a signal above the limit threshold and asserts output never exceeds the configured ceiling across the -40..+12 range.

requirement: Each hardware strip has a 6-cell stereo parametric EQ: Strip[i].EQ.channel[j].cell[k].on (0/1), .type (0-6: PEQ/NOTCH/BPF/LPF/HPF/LOSHELF/HISHELF), .f (20-20000 Hz), .gain (-36..+18 dB per Dec-2025 GUI/API range), .q (1-100), j=0-1 channels, k=0-5 cells; A/B memory banks via EQ.AB.
acceptance_test: Golden test configures each of the 7 filter types at representative frequency/gain/Q and asserts the measured frequency response matches a reference biquad-cascade implementation within tolerance across the full gain range.
notes: Gain range corrected in Dec 2025 release from API's stale -12/+12 to -36/+18; implement -36/+18.

feature: Strip EQ on/off and A/B compare
requirement: Strip[i].EQ.on toggles the whole 6-band EQ; EQ.AB (0/1) switches between two independently stored memory banks without audio glitch.
acceptance_test: Unit test stores different curves in A and B, toggles EQ.AB, and asserts the active curve switches accordingly with no discontinuity artifact beyond a documented click threshold.

requirement: Virtual strips expose a simple 3-band (bass/mid/treble) shelf/peak EQ, Strip[i].EQGain1/2/3, each -12..+12 dB.
acceptance_test: Golden test sweeps each band across its range and asserts the measured response matches a reference 3-band EQ model.

requirement: Strip[i].Label is a free-text string up to 60 UTF-8 bytes (per RT packet stripLabelUTF8c60[60]) used for strip identification in UI and telemetry.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets a 60-byte UTF-8 label including multi-byte characters and asserts it round-trips exactly; a 61+ byte label is truncated or rejected per spec.

requirement: Strip[i].A1..A5, .B1..B3 (0/1) independently route the strip to each of the 8 buses; toggled with += to flip.
acceptance_test: Unit test toggles each of the 8 assign bits independently and asserts only the enabled buses receive the strip's signal.

requirement: Strip[i].Reverb/.Delay/.Fx1/.Fx2 (0-10) set send levels to the internal reverb, internal delay (or C5), and two external FX aux paths; each has an independent PostReverb/PostDelay/PostFx1/PostFx2 (0/1) pre/post-fader tap point, available on hardware strips only.
acceptance_test: Property test sets each send 0-10 in both PRE and POST modes and asserts the send level tracks the fader in POST mode and is fader-independent in PRE mode.

requirement: Patch.insert[k] (k=0..33 on the Max channel set) toggles whether each of the 34 insert channels is routed through the pre-fader insert point.
acceptance_test: Unit test enables a subset of the 34 insert channels and asserts only those channels are exposed on/returned from the insert callback.

requirement: Patch.PostFxInsert (0=PRE default, 1=POST) selects whether the insert tap point sits before or after the strip's built-in FX chain (INTELLIPAN/comp/gate/denoiser/EQ), while always remaining pre-fader.
acceptance_test: Integration test asserts insert audio is unaffected by strip FX when PRE, and reflects strip FX processing when POST, in both cases arriving before the fader/mute stage.

requirement: Strip[i].App[k].Gain (0.0-1.0) and .App[k].Mute (0/1) control the first 4 (up to 11 shown) OS applications connected to a virtual strip's playback endpoint; Strip[i].AppGain/AppMute("name", value) address an app by name prefix match.
acceptance_test: Integration test opens two mock application audio sessions on a virtual strip, sets per-app gain/mute by index and by name, and asserts each session's rendered level responds independently.

requirement: Strip[i].device.name and .device.sr are read-only; .device.wdm/.ks/.mme/.asio are write-only device-name strings that (de)select the backend device for a physical strip; assigning "" unselects.
acceptance_test: Integration test selects a mock WDM/KS/MME device by name on a physical strip, asserts device.name and device.sr reflect it, then unselects with an empty string and asserts the strip falls back to NetAudio/ASIO-patch source.

requirement: Strip[i].VIO (0/1, physical strips only) enables the licensed VIO-extension virtual device as an alternate source for that hardware strip.
acceptance_test: Unit test toggles Strip[i].VIO and asserts the strip's audio source switches between the physical device path and the VIO-extension path.

requirement: EQ cell type field maps 0=PEQ (peaking), 1=NOTCH, 2=BPF (band-pass), 3=LPF (low-pass), 4=HPF (high-pass), 5=LOSHELF (low shelf), 6=HISHELF (high shelf).
acceptance_test: Unit test constructs each filter type at a fixed frequency and asserts its measured frequency-response shape (peak/notch/bandpass/lowpass/highpass/shelf) matches the documented category.

requirement: Bus[i].Mute (0/1) silences the entire bus output.
acceptance_test: Unit test mutes a bus and asserts zero output energy from that bus while other buses are unaffected.

requirement: Bus[i].Mono cycles 0 (off) -> 1 (mono: channels 1&2 merged) -> 2 (stereo reverse/cross: channels 1&2 swapped).
acceptance_test: Unit test sets each of the 3 states and asserts the documented channel behavior (identical L/R, or swapped L/R).

requirement: Bus[i].Gain accepts -60..+12 dB, default 0 dB.
acceptance_test: Property test sweeps the full range and asserts measured output level tracks target within tolerance.

requirement: Bus[i].FadeTo=(dB,ms) and Bus[i].FadeBy=(dB,ms) ramp bus gain identically to strip fades, 0-120000 ms.
acceptance_test: Unit test issues FadeTo/FadeBy on a bus and asserts the same ramp behavior validated for strips.

requirement: Bus[i].Label is a free-text string identifying the bus in UI/telemetry.
acceptance_test: Unit test round-trips a bus label string.

requirement: Bus[i].Sel (0/1, Max only) selects which bus's per-strip gain layer (GainLayer[j]) is currently shown/edited via the strip faders; CTRL+click-equivalent API call can select multiple buses simultaneously.
acceptance_test: Integration test selects two buses via Sel simultaneously and asserts both buses' gain layers are exposed as editable via the strip fader abstraction.

requirement: When Option.MonitorOnSEL is enabled, selecting a bus with SEL also routes that bus's audio to a configured Monitoring BUS (Bus[i].Monitor: 1 exclusive-select / 0 unselect-all).
acceptance_test: Integration test enables MonitorOnSEL, selects bus A3 with Sel, and asserts A3's audio is additionally summed into the configured monitoring bus.

requirement: A global Out Limiter option (default on) applies a brick-wall limiter to every bus output; when disabled, a simple non-limiting peak remover is applied instead.
acceptance_test: Golden test drives an over-range signal through a bus with the limiter on and off, asserting hard ceiling clamp in the on case and different (non-brick-wall) behavior in the off case.

spec_ref: PM p.71, p.107, p.112; API Option.delay[i]
requirement: Option.delay[i] provides 0-500 ms of output delay per physical bus (A1-A5), applied before the signal reaches physical, virtual, virtual-ASIO, and NetAudio outputs, extendable to 5000 ms via a configuration ceiling equivalent to MaxMonDelayMS.
acceptance_test: Property test sets delay across 0-500 ms (and up to 5000 ms with the ceiling raised) and asserts measured output latency increases by exactly the configured amount with sample accuracy, and that the delay is applied ahead of every documented output path.
notes: Dec 2025 change: delay now applies before virtual/NetAudio sends too, not just physical.

requirement: Bus[i].ReturnReverb, .ReturnDelay, .ReturnFx1, .ReturnFx2 (0-10 each) mix the internal reverb/delay(or C5)/external-FX1/external-FX2 return signal into each bus independently.
acceptance_test: Property test sets each return knob 0-10 and asserts the corresponding FX return signal is summed into that bus's output at a level tracking the knob value.

requirement: Bus[i].device.name/.sr are read-only; .wdm/.ks/.mme/.asio are write-only device-name strings; only A1 accepts .asio (ASIO output restricted to the main bus).
acceptance_test: Integration test asserts assigning .asio to a non-A1 bus is rejected/ignored while A1 accepts it, matching the documented ASIO-on-A1-only constraint.

requirement: Bus[i].VIO (0/1, physical bus only) enables routing that bus through the licensed VIO-extension output.
acceptance_test: Unit test toggles Bus[i].VIO and asserts the bus additionally/exclusively feeds the VIO-extension output path as documented.

feature: Bus EQ on/off and A/B memory
requirement: Bus[i].EQ.on toggles the 6-cell x 8-channel bus EQ; EQ.AB switches between two stored memory banks.
acceptance_test: Unit test verifies EQ bypass when off and correct bank switching between A/B without discontinuity beyond a documented click threshold.

requirement: Bus[i].EQ.channel[j].cell[k] (j=0-7 channels, k=0-5 cells) each has .on (0/1), .type (0-6), .f (20-20000 Hz), .gain (-36..+18 dB GUI range, documented API table shows -12..+12 — implement the wider -36..+18 GUI-matching range), .q (1-100).
acceptance_test: Golden test configures each of the 7 filter types on each of the 8 channels and asserts measured frequency response for each matches a reference cascade within tolerance across the full gain range.
notes: API PDF says -12..+12 but GUI/Dec-2025 notes say -36..+18; implement -36..+18 per corrected spine.

requirement: Bus[i].EQ.channel[j].Trim (-24..+24 dB) applies an independent master gain per bus channel, separate from the 6 EQ cells.
acceptance_test: Property test sweeps Trim across its range on one channel and asserts only that channel's level changes by the expected amount.

requirement: Bus[i].EQ.channel[j].Delay (0-500 ms) applies an independent time-alignment delay per bus channel, for surround speaker alignment.
acceptance_test: Property test sets Delay per channel and asserts measured inter-channel timing offsets match configured values with sample accuracy.

requirement: Each of a bus's 8 channels reports a status suitable for a 4-state LED: none applied, EQ-only applied, Delay-only applied, both applied.
acceptance_test: Unit test toggles EQ cells and Delay independently per channel and asserts the derived status enum matches all 4 documented combinations.

requirement: mode.normal passes all 8 bus channels through unmodified (pass-through).
acceptance_test: Golden test asserts bus output channels equal bus input channels sample-for-sample in Normal mode.

requirement: mode.Amix downmixes 5.1/7.1 to stereo with rear/side channels inverted to simulate a surround effect in stereo: LEFT = FL + 0.7*FC + SW + RL - SL; RIGHT = FR + 0.7*FC + SW - RR + SR.
acceptance_test: Golden test feeds known per-channel test tones and asserts the LEFT/RIGHT output matches the documented linear-combination formula within numeric tolerance.
notes: Manual's printed RIGHT formula uses 'RL' which the source flags as a likely typo for 'FR'; implement with FR and add a regression test pinning the corrected formula, documenting the discrepancy.

requirement: mode.Bmix downmixes to stereo with rear/side channels in phase: LEFT = FL + 0.7*FC + SW + RL + SL; RIGHT = FR + 0.7*FC + SW + RR + SR.
acceptance_test: Golden test verifies the formula against known per-channel inputs within numeric tolerance.

requirement: mode.Repeat copies the front stereo pair onto all 4 channel pairs: ch1,3,5,7 = FL; ch2,4,6,8 = FR (used with bus EQ LPF/HPF cells as an active crossover).
acceptance_test: Golden test asserts ch1/3/5/7 equal the FL input and ch2/4/6/8 equal the FR input exactly.

requirement: mode.Composite outputs the 8 bus channels as assigned by the global Composite Patch (Patch.composite[j], j=0-7), each channel sourced from a specific pre- or post-fader input channel (or the bus's own default channel).
acceptance_test: Integration test configures Patch.composite to source specific channels from named strips, selects Composite mode, and asserts the bus output matches the patched sources exactly, honoring Patch.PostFaderComposite pre/post selection.

requirement: mode.TVMix expands stereo to 7.1: FL=L, FR=R, FC=0.2*(L+R), SW=0.5*(L+R), RL=0.7*(L-R), RR=0.7*(R-L), SL=0.7*(L-R), SR=0.7*(R-L).
acceptance_test: Golden test verifies the formula against known L/R inputs within numeric tolerance.

requirement: mode.UpMix21: FL=L, FR=R, SW=0.5*(L+R); no center channel derived.
acceptance_test: Golden test verifies the formula against known L/R inputs.

requirement: mode.UpMix41: as Up Mix 2.1 plus RL=L, RR=R (rears are direct copies of front L/R).
acceptance_test: Golden test verifies the formula against known L/R inputs.

requirement: mode.UpMix61: as Up Mix 4.1 plus SL=L, SR=R (sides are direct copies of front L/R).
acceptance_test: Golden test verifies the formula against known L/R inputs.

requirement: mode.CenterOnly: LEFT=FC, RIGHT=FC (extracts the center channel to a stereo pair).
acceptance_test: Golden test asserts both output channels equal the FC input exactly.

requirement: mode.LFEOnly: LEFT=SW, RIGHT=SW (extracts the sub/LFE channel to a stereo pair).
acceptance_test: Golden test asserts both output channels equal the SW/LFE input exactly.

requirement: mode.RearOnly: LEFT=RL, RIGHT=RR (extracts the rear pair).
acceptance_test: Golden test asserts LEFT equals RL and RIGHT equals RR exactly.

requirement: When enabled, an up-mix bus mode auto-detects genuinely multichannel input (signal above -80 dBFS present on channel 3+) and skips the up-mix formula in that case, passing channels through instead.
acceptance_test: Unit test feeds silence-then-signal on channel 3 while in an up-mix mode with auto-detect enabled and asserts the engine switches from up-mix formula output to pass-through once the -80 dBFS threshold is crossed.

requirement: Patch.composite[j] (j=0-7) assigns each of the 8 composite channels to any input channel (pre- or post-fader per Patch.PostFaderComposite) or to the bus's own default channel (value 0).
acceptance_test: Unit test assigns each of the 8 composite channels to distinct source channels, toggles pre/post, and asserts the routing table resolves correctly in both modes.

spec_ref: PM p.40, p.70, p.91; API patch.OutA2..OutA5[i]
requirement: When A1 is an ASIO device and a physical bus A2-A5 has no device selected, patch.OutAx[i] (i=0-7) routes that bus's 8 channels onto arbitrary channels of the shared A1 ASIO device, in ascending bus order (A1,A2,A3,A4,A5) so a later bus overwrites an earlier one on overlapping channels.
acceptance_test: Integration test patches A2 and A3 to overlapping ASIO output channels and asserts the documented overwrite order (later bus wins) is reproduced deterministically.

requirement: When A1 is an ASIO device, patch.asio[i] (i=0-9, 2 per physical strip) maps ASIO input channels onto each hardware strip's L/R inputs.
acceptance_test: Integration test patches ASIO input channels to specific strips and asserts each strip receives audio from its patched channel pair.

requirement: Fx.Reverb.On (0/1) enables/disables the shared internal reverb send/return bus; Fx.Reverb.AB (0/1) switches between two stored memory banks.
acceptance_test: Unit test toggles Fx.Reverb.On and asserts reverb signal presence/absence on all sends; toggles AB and asserts curve switches without a hard discontinuity beyond a documented click threshold.

requirement: Fx.Delay.On/.AB control whichever effect currently occupies the Delay slot; System Settings selects at configuration time whether that slot is the MultiTap 8 delay or the C5 multiband compressor, and Delay.* API calls act on whichever is active.
acceptance_test: Unit test switches the Delay-slot selection between MultiTap and C5, then verifies Fx.Delay.On/.AB correctly enable/AB-switch whichever engine is currently loaded.

requirement: JustVerb III offers 3 room types (Plate, Room, Hall) x 3 sizes (Short, Med, Large) = 9 base room-type presets.
acceptance_test: Golden test loads each of the 9 room-type presets and asserts its impulse-response characteristics (early reflection density, decay envelope) match a stored reference within tolerance.

requirement: A preset block of 7 style presets (Vocal, Church, Stadium, Club, Soft, Pipe, Special) x 3 sizes (Short/Med/Large) = 21 presets, usable together with the 9 room-type presets for a documented '10 x 3 Preset' = 30 total combinations.
acceptance_test: Unit test recalls each of the documented preset combinations and asserts the resulting parameter set matches the stored preset table.

requirement: Dry and Wet knobs each range -inf..0..+6 dB, controlling the unprocessed and processed signal levels independently.
acceptance_test: Property test sweeps Dry and Wet independently and asserts each controls only its respective signal path level.

requirement: Pre-Delay knob ranges 0-1000 ms (0 default), delaying the onset of the reverb tail relative to the dry signal.
acceptance_test: Property test sets pre-delay across 0-1000 ms and asserts measured reverb-onset latency matches within sample tolerance.

requirement: E.Ref knob ranges Min..Max (0% default) controlling early-reflection amount in the reverb algorithm.
acceptance_test: Golden test measures early-reflection energy at Min/mid/Max settings against a reference model.

requirement: Decay knob ranges 0.5x-2x (1x = 100% = original preset time), scaling the reverb's decay/RT60 time.
acceptance_test: Golden test measures RT60 at 0.5x, 1x, 2x settings against a reference reverb decay-time model.

requirement: The reverb has its own 3-band full-parametric EQ (Hz/On/Gain/Q per band) applied to the reverb signal, plus a whole-EQ bypass.
acceptance_test: Golden test sweeps each of the 3 bands and asserts the reverb's spectral output responds as a parametric EQ would.

requirement: A BYP control fully bypasses the reverb engine (dry-only) without unloading its state.
acceptance_test: Unit test enables bypass and asserts output equals dry input with reverb tail absent, then disables and asserts prior reverb state resumes.

requirement: MultiTap 8 provides 8 independently configurable stereo taps, each with Delay time, Gain, Pan (L..C..R), Filter (Lo..Hi), Time Ratio, On, and Solo.
acceptance_test: Golden test configures each of the 8 taps with distinct delay/gain/pan and asserts the summed output contains 8 correctly-timed, panned, and filtered echoes of the input.

requirement: Left/Right balance knobs (L..C..R) re-balance the two input channels, enabling mono-sum or reverse-stereo treatment of the delay's input.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets balance to documented extremes and asserts the delay's internal input signal matches mono-sum or swapped-stereo behavior.

requirement: Pre Delay (0-1000 ms) delays the whole delay effect's input; Feedback (0-100%) loops the delay's output back into its input for repeating echoes.
acceptance_test: Property test sweeps Feedback and asserts echo decay rate follows feedback amount; sweeps Pre Delay and asserts first-tap onset time shifts accordingly.

requirement: Tap-tempo detection, Set Note (delay time by musical note duration at detected tempo), Auto Fit, Fix Delay, and Scale Fit implement a tempo-synced delay-time workflow.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates 4 tap-tempo inputs at a known BPM, invokes Set Note for a quarter note, and asserts the resulting tap delay time matches 60000/BPM ms within tolerance; Fix Delay locks in absolute ms and resets Time Ratio to 1.

requirement: Dry and Wet knobs (-inf..+6 dB each) mix the unprocessed and delayed signal at the effect's output.
acceptance_test: Property test sweeps Dry and Wet independently and asserts each controls only its respective path.

requirement: A Bypass control fully bypasses the delay engine (dry-only passthrough).
acceptance_test: Unit test enables bypass and asserts the delay tail disappears while dry signal continues.

requirement: C5 splits the signal into 5 bands via 4 configurable crossover frequencies.
acceptance_test: Golden test sets the 4 crossover points and asserts each band's measured passband matches the configured crossover frequencies within tolerance.

requirement: Each of the 5 bands independently has Gain (dB), Compressor on/off with Threshold/Ratio/Attack/Release/Knee/Out Gain, a Limiter with Limit level and Distortion (limiter reaction rate) control, plus Solo/Mute/Link.
acceptance_test: Property test sets each band's compressor/limiter parameters to documented bounds and asserts per-band gain reduction and limiting behavior matches a reference multiband model; Solo/Mute isolate the expected band.

requirement: A master Output Gain, Auto MakeUp, Bypass, and Link Type (ABS/REL/independent) control the combined 5-band output.
acceptance_test: Unit test verifies Bypass returns dry signal, Auto MakeUp compensates measured gain reduction, and Link Type ABS/REL change how per-band gain-reduction interacts across bands.

requirement: A strip whose signal is intended to pass through C5 must have all its direct bus-assign buttons off and use the POST send, since the C5 return re-enters via the bus; otherwise the dry strip signal doubles with the C5 return.
acceptance_test: Integration test wires a strip with a direct bus assignment AND a POST C5 send active, and asserts a documented double-signal condition is detectable/warned by validation logic (not silently produced).

feature: External FX 1/2 send/return (true AUX via ASIO)
requirement: Two true external AUX paths (Strip[i].Fx1/Fx2 sends, Bus[i].ReturnFx1/Fx2 returns) route through configurable stereo-pair channels of the ASIO device selected as bus A1, functioning only when A1 is an ASIO device with sufficient channels.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures Send1/Return1 to specific ASIO channel pairs on a mock multi-channel ASIO backend, round-trips a test signal through a loopback processor, and asserts the returned signal reaches the configured bus's ReturnFx1 mix point.

requirement: A dedicated single-client virtual ASIO device exposes all 34 pre-fader input channels for external (VST-host) processing, with per-strip 'i' insert-active indication and PRE/POST-FX tap selection (see routing area for the tap toggle).
acceptance_test: Integration test connects a mock single ASIO client to the insert device, verifies exactly 34 channels are exposed in/out in the documented per-strip order, that a second simultaneous client is refused (single-client constraint), and that the strip-level insert-active indicator reflects connection state.

requirement: The full 8x8 strip-to-bus routing matrix state (Strip[i].A1..B3) persists across engine restarts and settings load/save.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets a non-trivial routing pattern, restarts the engine (or reloads settings), and asserts the routing matrix is restored exactly.

requirement: Recorder.ArmStrip(i) arms one or more strips as a pre-fader recording source, mixed to stereo, unaffected by fader/FX/mute/solo state.
acceptance_test: Integration test arms two strips, mutes one of them, and asserts the recorded signal still contains both strips' full-level pre-fader content.

requirement: Recorder.ArmBus(i) arms a bus (2-8 channels, honoring Composite mode) as a post-fader ('what you hear') recording source, including buses with no physical/virtual device attached (record-only bus).
acceptance_test: Integration test arms a Composite-mode bus with no output device, feeds it via the Composite Patch, and asserts the recorder captures the composited signal correctly.

feature: Recorder mode: record inputs vs record bus
requirement: Recorder.mode.recbus (0=record armed strip inputs, 1=record armed bus) selects which arming set is active for the current recording.
acceptance_test: Unit test toggles recbus and asserts the recorder switches between the ArmStrip and ArmBus signal sources.

requirement: Devices are enumerated and presented grouped by audio interface type (WDM, KS, MME, ASIO) and sorted alphabetically by driver name within each group.
acceptance_test: Unit test enumerates a mock device list of mixed types and asserts the returned/display order groups by interface type then alphabetically.

requirement: Device enumeration reports device type as MME=1, WDM=3, KS=4, ASIO=5 (ASIO only for outputs, restricted to bus A1).
acceptance_test: Unit test enumerates mock devices of each type and asserts the reported type constants match the documented mapping, with ASIO devices offered only for bus A1's output selector.

requirement: Physical (hardware) input strips accept WDM, KS, MME devices only (no ASIO device selection), across 8-192 kHz, mono or stereo.
acceptance_test: Integration test attempts to assign an ASIO device to a hardware strip's input selector and asserts it is rejected, while WDM/KS/MME devices across the documented rate range are accepted.

feature: Physical output A1 interface set (incl. ASIO)
requirement: Bus A1 accepts WDM, KS, MME, or ASIO devices across 32-192 kHz, 1-8 channels; ASIO device selection is exclusive to A1.
acceptance_test: Integration test assigns an ASIO device to A1 and asserts acceptance; asserts the same ASIO device assignment to A2-A5 is rejected/ignored.

requirement: Buses A2-A5 accept WDM, KS, MME devices only, 8-192 kHz, 1-8 channels.
acceptance_test: Integration test assigns WDM/KS/MME devices to A2-A5 and asserts acceptance across the documented rate range.

requirement: The 3 virtual input strips accept WDM, KS, MME, DirectX, WaveRT application-facing formats, 1-8 channels, 8-192 kHz; virtual outputs expose 2 channels by default (up to 8 via KS).
acceptance_test: Integration test opens a virtual strip's endpoint via each supported application API and asserts the documented channel-count and rate constraints.

requirement: WDM and KS playback devices are opened in exclusive mode by default, bypassing the OS mixer.
acceptance_test: Integration test opens a mock WDM output device and asserts the backend requests exclusive mode by default; a configuration flag can force shared mode.

requirement: WDM input devices are driven in shared mode by default to avoid a documented WASAPI exclusive-mode instability; an experimental input-exclusive mode exists but is disabled by default.
acceptance_test: Integration test opens a mock WDM input device and asserts shared mode is requested by default; enabling the experimental flag switches to exclusive mode.

feature: Engine SWIFT mode (experimental, disabled by default)
requirement: An experimental low-latency WDM engine mode (SWIFT) exists behind a configuration flag, disabled by default and not exposed in the main UI.
acceptance_test: Unit test asserts the SWIFT flag defaults to off and, when enabled programmatically, changes the WDM I/O path's internal buffering strategy per a documented low-latency mode.
notes: Marked disabled/experimental upstream; keep as an internal flag only, not a UI-exposed default path.

requirement: Option.ASIOsr (0=use ASIO driver's current default rate, 1=force the Preferred Main Sample Rate) governs whether the engine tries to force a specific rate on the ASIO driver.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets Option.ASIOsr=1 with a mock ASIO driver whose current rate differs from the preferred rate and asserts the engine requests a rate change; with =0 asserts no rate-change request is made.

requirement: Option.buffer.asio (0=driver default, else 128-2048 forced) governs the ASIO buffer size request; the driver may refuse a forced value.
acceptance_test: Integration test requests a forced buffer size on a mock ASIO driver that accepts it and one that refuses it, and asserts the engine surfaces the resulting actual buffer size in both cases.

requirement: An option automatically restarts the audio engine when the device assigned to bus A1 is disconnected.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates A1 device removal on the null/mock backend with the option enabled and asserts the engine performs a full restart cycle and resumes streaming once a device is available.

requirement: An option automatically restarts the audio engine when any assigned input or output device (not just A1) is disconnected.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates disconnect of a non-A1 device with the option enabled and asserts a full engine restart cycle occurs.

requirement: A configurable countdown (default 5 s) delays engine start at launch to allow devices time to become ready; a device not ready within the window is treated as unavailable until the next manual restart.
acceptance_test: Integration test starts the engine with a mock device that becomes ready 3s and 7s after launch respectively, against a 5s countdown, and asserts the 3s device is picked up and the 7s device is not until a manual restart.

requirement: Three OS-level virtual playback (recording-source) endpoints feed virtual strips 6, 7, 8 respectively, discoverable by name in the OS sound settings.
acceptance_test: Integration test on each supported OS backend creates the 3 virtual playback endpoints, plays audio into each from a mock application, and asserts it arrives on the corresponding virtual strip.

requirement: Three OS-level virtual recording endpoints expose buses B1, B2, B3 respectively as capturable sources for other applications.
acceptance_test: Integration test feeds known audio to each bus and asserts a mock recording application opening the corresponding endpoint captures it correctly.

requirement: A licensed-in-original/optional-in-OPENMIX extension exposes 5 additional virtual playback endpoints mapped to hardware strips 1-5 and 5 additional virtual recording endpoints mapped to buses A1-A5.
acceptance_test: Integration test enables the extension and asserts the 5+5 additional endpoints appear and route to/from the documented strips/buses.

requirement: Each virtual I/O's internal ring-buffer latency is independently configurable, must be at least 3x the engine's current buffer size for stability, defaults to 7168 samples, and applies symmetrically to the paired playback and recording endpoint.
acceptance_test: Property test sets the engine buffer size and asserts the virtual I/O latency setter enforces/warns on the 3x-buffer-size floor; verifies changing a virtual input's latency also changes its paired output's latency.

requirement: A default-on loopback mode lets an application capture a virtual playback endpoint's own played audio directly (e.g. for screen-recording/streaming tools), without needing to route through a bus.
acceptance_test: Integration test plays audio into a virtual playback endpoint and asserts a mock capture client can read it back directly via loopback, without any bus routing configured.

requirement: OS master/application volume has no effect on a virtual playback endpoint's level unless an explicit 'enable OS volume control' setting is turned on; virtual recording endpoints (bus outputs) provide no OS-level gain control at all.
acceptance_test: Integration test changes the OS volume for a virtual playback endpoint with the gating option off/on and asserts engine-side level is unaffected/affected respectively; asserts no OS gain control is exposed for recording endpoints.

requirement: Each of the 3 virtual strips exposes a virtual ASIO device with 8 channels in/out and up to 4 simultaneous client applications; a client's output is summed into that virtual strip's input alongside any OS-application audio already present.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects up to 4 mock ASIO clients to one virtual-strip's ASIO device, asserts a 5th connection is refused, and asserts each client's output is summed correctly into the strip.

requirement: Sample rate and buffer size for all virtual ASIO devices are dictated by bus A1's current device configuration, not independently settable.
acceptance_test: Integration test changes A1's sample rate/buffer and asserts all three virtual ASIO devices report the new configuration to their clients.

feature: Virtual ASIO adds one buffer of latency
requirement: Connecting a client to a virtual ASIO device adds exactly one A1-buffer-size worth of processing latency to that signal path.
acceptance_test: Integration test measures round-trip latency with and without a virtual ASIO client connected and asserts the delta equals one A1 buffer period within tolerance.

requirement: The 34-channel insert ASIO device accepts exactly one connected client at a time; a second connection attempt is refused.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects one mock client, attempts a second, and asserts the second connection is refused with a documented error.

requirement: On the Windows target, a single virtual-device driver instance exposes all 8 I/O pairs (5 extension + 3 core), rather than 3+ separate driver instances.
acceptance_test: Integration test on the Windows virtual-device backend enumerates installed virtual drivers and asserts exactly one combined driver instance is present exposing 8 I/O pairs.

requirement: Each virtual endpoint independently negotiates/exposes its own OS-level sample rate and bit depth (default 48 kHz), settable per endpoint from the OS sound control panel equivalent, independent of the engine's internal processing rate.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets a virtual endpoint's OS-facing format to 48 kHz/16-bit while the engine runs internally at 44.1 kHz/24-bit and asserts correct SRC/bit-depth conversion occurs transparently.

feature: ASIO restricted to bus A1 for output device selection
requirement: Only bus A1 may have an ASIO device selected as its output; all other buses and all physical strip inputs reach ASIO hardware only via channel patching against the A1 ASIO device.
acceptance_test: Integration test attempts ASIO device assignment on A2-A5 and on a hardware strip and asserts rejection, while patch-based routing (patch.OutAx / patch.asio) succeeds against the A1 device.

requirement: The build never bundles the Steinberg ASIO SDK; ASIO backend support is compiled only when a locally supplied SDK path is provided by the person building, and the default CI/OSS build excludes ASIO entirely.
acceptance_test: CI test asserts a default build (no SDK path provided) compiles and links successfully with the ASIO backend feature disabled; a documented build with SDK path set enables it.

requirement: When multiple buses are patched onto overlapping ASIO output channels, the last-processed bus in ascending order (A1,A2,A3,A4,A5) wins on any overlapping channel.
acceptance_test: Integration test patches A1 and A4 onto the same ASIO output channel and asserts A4's signal is what actually reaches that channel.

requirement: Selecting an ASIO device as A1 allows launching that driver's native control panel from within the mixer's device settings UI.
acceptance_test: Manual/e2e test opens the device settings for an A1 ASIO device and asserts a control-panel launch action is available and invokes the driver's panel entry point.

feature: ASIO warning dialog on A1 assignment
requirement: Selecting an ASIO device for bus A1 surfaces a one-time informational warning about the ASIO-only-on-A1 and patch-based routing model before committing the change.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test selects an ASIO device for A1 and asserts the warning dialog appears exactly once per session/assignment.

requirement: Virtual ASIO devices report a configurable sample format (documented default Float32LSB, with Int32LSB as an alternative for host compatibility).
acceptance_test: Integration test negotiates each supported sample format with a mock ASIO host and asserts correct bit-exact conversion in both directions.
notes: Vendor reference notes a real-world Float32LSB interop issue with one DAW; keep Int32LSB switchable as a compatibility escape hatch.

requirement: Buffer sizes below 256 samples at 44.1/48 kHz on the ASIO path are permitted but flagged as a stability risk in diagnostics.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets a 128-sample ASIO buffer and asserts a stability-risk diagnostic event is raised (matching engine-wide buffer-floor behavior).

requirement: System settings expose 4 independent stereo-pair ASIO channel selectors (Send1, Return1, Send2, Return2) that only take effect when bus A1 is an ASIO device with enough channels.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures all 4 selectors on a mock multi-channel ASIO A1 device and asserts strip sends/bus returns route through the selected channel pairs exactly.

requirement: The recorder supports REW, PLAY, STOP, FF, REC (toggles to PAUSE while recording, resuming into the same file), REPLAY (seek to 0, honors Loop), and GOTO(hh:mm:ss).
acceptance_test: Integration test drives each transport command via the control API against a mock file source/sink and asserts correct state transitions and, for GOTO, sample-accurate seek.

requirement: Command.Eject releases the currently loaded/recording file handle so other processes can access it, and can be invoked while actively recording.
acceptance_test: Integration test issues Eject mid-recording and asserts the file is closed/flushed and externally readable immediately, while the recorder returns to an idle state.

requirement: Recorder.FileType selects WAV (1), AIFF (2), BWF (3), or MP3 (100); MP3 is stereo-only at 32-320 kbps, other formats support 1-8 channels.
acceptance_test: Property test records a multichannel bus in WAV/AIFF/BWF and asserts channel count up to 8 is preserved; asserts MP3 recording of a >2 channel source is downmixed or rejected per documented stereo-only constraint.

requirement: The recorder can play back WAV, AIFF, MP3, M4A, MP4, MOV, AVI, WMA, WMV files (audio track extracted for video containers).
acceptance_test: Integration test loads one sample file of each documented format and asserts successful playback with correct duration/sample count reported.

requirement: Recorder.bitResolution accepts 8, 16, 24, or 32 (32 = IEEE float).
acceptance_test: Property test records at each of the 4 bit depths and asserts the resulting file's bit depth matches, with 32 verified as float sample format.

requirement: Recorder.Channel accepts 1-8 channels for non-MP3 formats.
acceptance_test: Property test records at each channel count 1-8 and asserts the resulting file has the correct channel count.

requirement: Recorder.kbps sets the MP3 encoding bitrate; the vendor-documented set is 32,40,48,56,64,80,96,112,128,160,192,224,256,320 kbps.
acceptance_test: Property test encodes MP3 at each documented bitrate and asserts the resulting file's bitrate matches within encoder tolerance.

feature: Recorder sample rate independent of engine
requirement: The recorder's target file sample rate is independently configurable from the engine's internal processing/master sample rate, with automatic conversion applied.
acceptance_test: Integration test records at a file sample rate different from the engine's internal rate and asserts the output file's actual sample rate and pitch/duration are correct.

requirement: Recording in WAV/AIFF/MP3 auto-stops at a 2 GiB file-size limit (RIFF 32-bit size field constraint); BWF format is exempt from this limit.
acceptance_test: Integration test drives a synthetic long recording past the 2 GiB boundary in WAV and asserts the recorder auto-stops cleanly with a valid, playable file; the same scenario in BWF continues recording past 2 GiB.

requirement: Default output filenames follow '<prefix> YYYY-MM-DD at HHhMMmSSs.<ext>' with a configurable prefix (default 'Record') and a configurable target directory.
acceptance_test: Unit test freezes the clock, sets a custom prefix, triggers a new recording, and asserts the generated filename matches the exact documented pattern and extension for the selected format.

requirement: When Recorder.mode.MultiTrack is enabled, one additional mono file per channel (suffix _Track1, _Track2, ... up to 8) is written alongside (or instead of) the interleaved file.
acceptance_test: Integration test records an 8-channel bus with MultiTrack enabled and asserts 8 correctly-named, correctly-content mono files are produced in addition to/instead of the interleaved file.

requirement: A continuously-running pre-recording ring buffer (0 = off, up to a configurable maximum, default 20 s, configurable up to 60 s) lets REC capture audio from before the button was pressed.
acceptance_test: Integration test lets the ring buffer accumulate 15s of audio, presses REC, and asserts the resulting file begins 15s before the REC press timestamp (bounded by the configured buffer size).

requirement: recorder.A1..A5, .B1..B3 (0/1 each) independently route recorder playback output to any combination of the 8 buses.
acceptance_test: Unit test enables a subset of the 8 routing bits during playback and asserts only those buses receive the playback signal.

requirement: Recorder.gain (-60..+12 dB) sets the recorder's playback output level independent of the recording level.
acceptance_test: Property test sweeps playback gain across its range and asserts measured playback output level tracks target.

feature: Playback modes: Play On Load, Loop, timed stop
requirement: Recorder.mode.PlayOnLoad auto-starts playback when a file is loaded; Recorder.mode.Loop restarts playback at end-of-file; a configurable duration timer (0 = disabled) stops an in-progress recording automatically.
acceptance_test: Integration test loads a file with PlayOnLoad enabled and asserts playback auto-starts; enables Loop and asserts playback restarts at EOF; sets a stop-after-duration timer during recording and asserts auto-stop at the configured time.

requirement: Recorder.load (write-only string) loads a named playback file; Recorder.Prefix (write-only string) sets the filename prefix used for new recordings.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets Recorder.load to a known file path and asserts playback of that exact file; sets Recorder.Prefix and asserts the next recorded filename uses it.

requirement: The current arming state (which strips or buses are armed) is queryable via the control API and persists in saved settings.
acceptance_test: Integration test arms a mix of strips/buses, saves settings, reloads, and asserts the exact arming state is restored and reported correctly via the get-parameter API.

requirement: Transport state changes (PLAY, STOP, REC, and End-Of-File) are published as discrete events consumable by the macro/automation layer.
acceptance_test: Integration test subscribes to transport events, drives the recorder through play/stop/record and to end-of-file on a short test clip, and asserts each documented event fires exactly once at the correct transition.

feature: MIDI device selection (primary + extra input + output)
requirement: The MIDI mapping subsystem supports one primary MIDI input device, one secondary 'MIDI Extra Input Device', and one MIDI output device used for feedback, selectable independently.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects mock MIDI devices to each of the 3 roles and asserts input from either input device reaches the mapping engine and feedback is sent only to the configured output device.

requirement: A Learn mode lets the user select a target control, move a physical MIDI control, and have that MIDI code bound to the control; TAB/up/down navigate to the next/previous control while Learn is active; clicking the code display resets a binding.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test enters Learn mode, sends a synthetic MIDI CC message, and asserts the CC is bound to the currently-selected control; asserts navigating with TAB moves the learn target and a reset clears a binding.

requirement: Mappable controls include strip gain faders, mute, solo, M.C., audibility, 3-band EQ, transport (tape) controls, denoiser, reverb/delay/FX1/FX2 sends, SEL, and the first 4 virtual-strip application volumes; comp/gate/denoiser/pitch detail parameters are MIDI-mappable per later releases.
acceptance_test: Unit test binds a MIDI CC to each category of mappable control and asserts the corresponding parameter responds to incoming MIDI values scaled to its documented range.

requirement: Feedback mode F sends MIDI feedback only when a control changes via a non-MIDI source (mouse, script, NetAudio); mode FF additionally echoes feedback back to the originating MIDI controller (for LED buttons/motorized faders).
acceptance_test: Integration test changes a mapped control via script and asserts feedback is sent in F mode; changes the same control via MIDI input and asserts no echo occurs in F mode but does occur in FF mode.

requirement: Per-control feedback values for 2-position controls are independently configurable (default 127 ON / 0 OFF), including arbitrary custom MIDI messages such as SysEx, for driving LCDs or machine-control surfaces.
acceptance_test: Unit test configures custom ON/OFF feedback values (including a SysEx payload) for a mapped mute button and asserts the exact configured bytes are transmitted on each state change.

requirement: Duplicate MIDI feedback assignments (two controls mapped to send the same MIDI message) are visually flagged so the user can find the first conflicting binding.
acceptance_test: Unit test creates two feedback bindings using the identical MIDI message and asserts both are flagged as conflicting, with a lookup returning the first-bound control.

requirement: A Refresh Controller action re-sends all feedback messages reflecting current mixer state, and is itself assignable as a MIDI-triggerable function.
acceptance_test: Integration test triggers Refresh Controller and asserts feedback messages for every currently-mapped control are (re)transmitted once, matching current parameter values.

requirement: A PTT binding un-mutes a strip while a MIDI control is held and re-mutes on release.
acceptance_test: Integration test binds PTT to a strip, sends MIDI note-on then note-off for the mapped control, and asserts the strip un-mutes on note-on and re-mutes on note-off.

requirement: The complete MIDI mapping (all learned bindings + feedback options) can be saved to and loaded from a named file, and reset to empty in one action.
acceptance_test: Integration test creates several bindings, saves the map, resets, reloads, and asserts every binding is restored exactly.

requirement: A control-API function returns raw MIDI bytes (2-3 byte messages, up to a documented buffer size) received on the mapped input device, and another sends raw MIDI bytes to the mapped output device.
acceptance_test: Unit test sends a synthetic 3-byte MIDI message to the mapped input and asserts the raw-read API returns the exact bytes; sends via the raw-write API and asserts the mapped output device receives them unmodified.

requirement: MIDI messages arriving over the NetAudio-MIDI incoming stream are treated identically to a physical MIDI input device by the mapping engine and are also forwarded to the macro/automation layer.
acceptance_test: Integration test sends a MIDI message over a mock NetAudio-MIDI stream and asserts it triggers the same mapped-control response as the equivalent physical MIDI input, and is also observable by a macro-layer listener.

spec_ref: PM p.74, p.95; API netaudio.outstream[8].route bitmask
requirement: An outgoing NetAudio-MIDI stream can be sourced from MIDI-in, MIDI-aux-in, incoming NetAudio-MIDI, and/or MIDI-out feedback via an OR-able bitmask (0x01/0x02/0x04/0x08), so MIDI feedback or forwarded MIDI reaches remote devices.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets each individual bit and combinations (including ALL=0x07) and asserts exactly the selected sources are relayed onto the outgoing NetAudio-MIDI stream.

requirement: Outgoing/incoming packets use the 4-byte magic value matching the incumbent's 'VBAN'-compatible identifier so plain audio streams interoperate with existing NetAudio/VBAN-family senders and receivers.
acceptance_test: Interop test sends a packet built by a third-party VBAN-compatible sender to the OPENMIX receiver and asserts it decodes correctly, and vice versa.

requirement: The header is exactly 28 bytes, little-endian, tightly packed: 4-byte magic, format_SR (5-bit rate index + 3-bit sub-protocol), format_nbs (samples/frame minus 1), format_nbc (channels minus 1), format_bit (3-bit data type + reserved bit + 4-bit codec), 16-byte ASCII stream name, 4-byte little-endian frame counter.
acceptance_test: Unit test constructs a header field-by-field and asserts the serialized byte layout matches the documented offsets/sizes exactly, and that a fuzzed 28-byte buffer round-trips through parse+serialize without panicking.
Property test maps each of the 21 defined indices to its documented rate and asserts round-trip encode/decode; asserts an undefined index (21-31) is rejected or flagged.

requirement: format_SR bits 5-7 select the sub-protocol: 0x00 AUDIO, 0x20 SERIAL, 0x40 TXT, 0x60 SERVICE, 0x80 FRAME (undefined-1 slot repurposed), 0xA0/0xC0 undefined, 0xE0 USER.
acceptance_test: Unit test constructs a header for each of the 5 implemented sub-protocol codes and asserts the receiver dispatches to the correct handler; unknown codes are safely ignored/logged.

requirement: format_bit bits 0-2 select data type (0 BYTE8, 1 INT16, 2 INT24, 3 INT32, 4 FLOAT32, 5 FLOAT64, 6 12-bit int, 7 10-bit int); bit 3 is reserved and must be 0; bits 4-7 select codec (0x00 PCM implemented; VNCA/VNCV/reserved/USER rejected as unsupported).
acceptance_test: Property test encodes/decodes audio in each of the 8 data-type formats with PCM codec and asserts bit-accurate round trip; a packet with reserved bit 3 set is treated as corrupt.

requirement: Maximum UDP payload for NetAudio data is 1436 bytes (1464-byte packet, reserving headroom for VLAN tags within the 1500-byte Ethernet MTU) and maximum samples per packet is 256, whichever is smaller given channel count and bit depth.
acceptance_test: Property test computes max samples/packet for representative channel-count/bit-depth combinations and asserts the sender never exceeds either the 1436-byte payload cap or the 256-sample cap.

requirement: Audio sample data is interleaved by channel exactly as in a standard WAV file; a receiver must verify received byte count matches the expected size for the declared format and treat a mismatch as corrupt.
acceptance_test: Unit test sends interleaved PCM at 1,2,8 channels and asserts correct de-interleaving; a truncated/oversized payload is flagged as a Corrupt error.

requirement: A monotonically increasing 32-bit frame counter in each packet is used by the receiver to detect and correct stream discontinuities (dropped or reordered packets).
acceptance_test: Unit test replays a sequence with a deliberate counter gap and out-of-order packet and asserts the receiver's Missing/Disorder error counters increment as documented and the audio output is repaired per the documented discontinuity-correction strategy.

requirement: Incoming jitter-buffer size in samples is computed as 3 x max(current negotiated buffer, quality-level minimum), floored at 6x256=1536 samples, with quality-level minimums Optimal>=512, Fast>=1024, Medium>=2048, Slow>=4096, Very Slow>=8192.
acceptance_test: Property test computes the stack size for each of the 5 quality levels at representative current-buffer sizes and asserts the result exactly matches the documented formula, including the 1536-sample floor.

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.12; PM p.55
requirement: Per-stream Net Quality is selectable among Optimal (0), Fast (1), Medium (2), Slow (3), Very Slow (4), trading latency for jitter tolerance.
acceptance_test: Integration test runs an incoming stream at each quality level under simulated jitter and asserts underrun/overload error rates decrease as quality level increases from Optimal to Very Slow.

requirement: The SERIAL sub-protocol carries a bps-index in format_SR bits 0-4 (25-entry table), a channel/pipe identifier in format_nbc (up to 256 virtual pipes), COM-mode bits in format_nbs (stop bits, start/parity flags, multi-packet flag for SysEx >1436B), and a serial-type nibble in format_bit bits 4-7 (0x00 GENERIC, 0x10 MIDI, ... 0xF0 USER); MIDI packets carry one or more complete messages under 1436 bytes.
acceptance_test: Interop test sends a multi-message MIDI SERIAL packet and a multi-packet SysEx (bit 7 set) sequence and asserts correct MIDI message reconstruction on the receiver.

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.17-18; PM p.72
requirement: The TXT sub-protocol carries a bps index, a channel/pipe identifier (format_nbc), and a text-encoding nibble in format_bit bits 4-7 (0x00 ASCII, 0x10 UTF8, 0x20 WCHAR, ... 0xF0 USER); a single complete script/command message must be under 1436 bytes and uses the same request grammar as the control API/macro scripts.
acceptance_test: Interop test sends a UTF-8 TEXT packet containing a valid parameter-set script (e.g. mute+gain requests) to a mock 'Command1' stream and asserts the parameters are applied exactly as if set via the local control API.

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.19-20; PM p.58
requirement: The FRAME sub-protocol links multiple packets into one frame for payloads exceeding 1436 bytes using a Mbps-index in format_SR bits 0-4 (25-entry table), a 16-bit packet index split across format_nbs (LSB)/format_nbc (MSB), and start/continue/end flags in format_bit bits 0-2; a frame with any missing packet is dropped entirely.
acceptance_test: Unit test reassembles a multi-packet PNG/JPG frame from start/continue/end packets and asserts correct reassembly; a sequence missing one continuation packet results in the whole frame being dropped, not corrupted output.

requirement: An outgoing FRAME stream can source the main app view or one of up to 4 displays (4K max), encode as PNG or JPG at 1-30 fps, JPG quality 1-100%, optional cursor capture, and a configurable theoretical bandwidth cap (default 12 Mbps, non-enforcing).
acceptance_test: Integration test configures each source/format/fps/quality combination against a mock 4K display capture and asserts the produced frame stream matches the configured parameters (format, approximate fps, cursor presence).

requirement: The SERVICE sub-protocol (format_SR fixed at the SERVICE code) dispatches on a service-type field in format_nbc (0 IDENTIFICATION/PING, 1 CHATUTF8, 32 RTPACKETREGISTER, 33 RTPACKET) and a function/reply field in format_nbs (bits 0-6 function id, bit 7 = reply flag).
acceptance_test: Unit test constructs SERVICE packets for each of the 4 documented service types and asserts the receiver dispatches to the correct handler and correctly distinguishes request vs. reply via bit 7.

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.22-24; PM p.56
requirement: A PING request/reply carries a fixed-layout identification structure (capability bitmask, preferred/min/max rate, device/app/host/user names, optional GPS/user position) and a peer must reply to any structurally valid PING (even an all-zero payload) with its own identification.
acceptance_test: Interop test sends a minimal (zeroed) PING0 payload to the engine's SERVICE listener and asserts a valid PING0 reply is returned containing the engine's own identification fields; malformed/undersized PING payloads are ignored, not crashed on.

requirement: PING bitType flags identify device roles (RECEPTOR 0x1, TRANSMITTER 0x2, RECEPTORSPOT 0x4, TRANSMITTERSPOT 0x8, VIRTUALDEVICE 0x10, VIRTUALMIXER 0x20, MATRIX 0x40, DAW 0x80, SERVER 0x01000000) and bitfeature flags identify supported sub-protocols (AUDIO 0x1, AOIP 0x2, VOIP 0x4, SERIAL 0x100, MIDI 0x300, FRAME 0x1000, TXT 0x10000).
acceptance_test: Unit test builds a PING reply for the engine and asserts the bitType/bitfeature fields accurately reflect the engine's actual enabled sub-protocols and role (VIRTUALMIXER | AUDIO|SERIAL|MIDI|TXT|FRAME as applicable).

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.24; PM p.56-57
requirement: The CHAT service type carries UTF-8 text messages (plus nudge/alert variants) between identified peers, independent of and resilient to audio-stream failure (e.g. firewall blocking audio but not chat).
acceptance_test: Interop test exchanges CHAT messages between two mock peers while the AUDIO sub-protocol is deliberately blocked, and asserts CHAT delivery is unaffected.

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.24-25; PM RT service
requirement: A client subscribes to real-time telemetry via an RTPACKETREGISTER request specifying a timeout (0-255 s) and an optional list of up to 128 packet IDs (all IDs if omitted); the server replies 0 (bad/unknown id), 1 (registered), or 2 (busy/no slot); the client must re-register before the timeout elapses or the subscription lapses, and up to 8 concurrent RT-packet clients are supported.
acceptance_test: Integration test registers with a 15s timeout, asserts packets flow, lets the timeout lapse without renewal and asserts packets stop; asserts a 9th simultaneous subscriber receives a busy (2) reply when 8 slots are already used.

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.25; MixboardRemote.h T_NETAUDIO_MXRT_PACKET
requirement: Packet ID 0 delivers, in one fixed-layout struct, mixer type/version/samplerate, per-input pre-fader peak levels (34), per-output peak levels (64), a transport-state bitfield, per-strip and per-bus state bitfields (mute/solo/mono/mute-center/EQ/bus-mode/routing/pan-panel/post-fx/SEL/monitor flags), per-strip gain-layer values (8 buses x 8 strips), per-bus gain, and UTF-8 labels (up to 60 bytes) for all 8 strips and 8 buses.
acceptance_test: Unit test serializes a known mixer state into packet 0 and asserts every documented field decodes back to the exact original state on a reference client; a fuzzed packet of the wrong size is rejected without panic.

spec_ref: NetAudio Protocol Specifications rev 13 (SEP 2025) p.25; MixboardRemote.h T_NETAUDIO_VMPARAMSTRIP_PACKET
requirement: Packet ID 1 delivers per-strip detailed parameters for all 8 strips (mode, level, audibility, 3D/color/mod pan positions, 3-band EQ gains, first-channel 6-band PEQ state, FX send levels, limiter value, karaoke mode, full compressor/gate parameter sets, denoiser threshold, pitch/voice-modeler bitfield and values), useful for building a full remote strip-detail UI without polling every parameter individually.
acceptance_test: Unit test serializes a known per-strip detail state into packet 1 and asserts every documented field decodes back exactly on a reference client.

requirement: Each of 8 incoming and 8 outgoing audio streams independently configures on/off, a 16-char stream name, source/destination IP (hostname-resolvable), UDP port, quality level, and a routing target (incoming: destination strip 0-8; outgoing: source bus 0-8); outgoing streams additionally set sample rate (11025-96000 Hz list), channel count (1-8) and bit depth (16 or 24-bit PCM).
acceptance_test: Integration test configures all 8 outgoing streams with distinct names/IPs/ports/rates/channels and asserts each produces correctly-addressed, correctly-formatted packets independently; configures all 8 incoming streams and asserts each routes to its configured destination strip.

requirement: Toggling netaudio.Enable, or changing an incoming stream's port or quality, or an outgoing stream's quality, requires (and triggers) an audio-engine restart to take effect.
acceptance_test: Integration test changes each of the documented restart-inducing parameters individually and asserts an engine-restart event is triggered exactly once per change; changing a non-restart-inducing parameter (e.g. stream name) does not trigger a restart.

requirement: An incoming audio stream is uniquely identified by the combination of stream name, source IP, and UDP port; two applications on the same host cannot bind the same UDP port simultaneously.
acceptance_test: Integration test attempts to bind two local NetAudio listeners to the same UDP port and asserts the second bind fails with a clear, documented error rather than silently stealing packets.

requirement: An outgoing stream may be addressed to a subnet broadcast address (x.x.x.255) to reach all receivers on a wired LAN segment in one send; broadcast is not expected to traverse typical Wi-Fi access points.
acceptance_test: Interop test sends to a broadcast address on a simulated wired LAN and asserts multiple mock receivers on that subnet all receive the stream from one send.

requirement: Each incoming stream independently tracks 5 distinct error conditions: Overload (packets arriving faster than consumed, early clock), Corrupt (malformed payload), Disorder (out-of-sequence packets), Missing (lost packets), and Underrun (packets arriving too slowly or stopped, late clock).
acceptance_test: Integration test injects each error condition individually (burst delivery, malformed packet, reordering, dropped packet, stalled delivery) against a mock receiver and asserts exactly the corresponding counter increments.

spec_ref: PM p.54; developer forum notes in reference doc
requirement: Each incoming NetAudio stream runs its own sample-rate-conversion stage to reconcile the sender's independent (unsynchronized) clock with the engine's master sample rate, since the protocol carries no clock/sync information.
acceptance_test: Integration test feeds an incoming stream at a deliberately drifted sample rate (e.g. +50 ppm) relative to engine rate and asserts no audible pitch drift or accumulating buffer over/underflow over a multi-minute test run.

feature: Default UDP port and firewall prompt
requirement: The NetAudio service binds UDP port 6980 by default, configurable per stream, and its first-run firewall prompt is a documented, expected part of setup on Windows.
acceptance_test: Integration test starts the NetAudio service with default configuration and asserts it binds to UDP 6980; a documented flag allows all-stream port override.

requirement: A thin C-ABI-compatible shared library exposes the same exported function names/signatures as the incumbent's Remote API DLL, so existing third-party wrappers/Stream Deck/Companion-style plugins load and function against OPENMIX without modification.
acceptance_test: Integration test loads an unmodified third-party wrapper binary/DLL-consumer against the OPENMIX shim and asserts login, parameter get/set, and level queries behave identically to the documented incumbent contract.

requirement: A login function establishes a client session (return codes distinguishing OK, 'OK but app not running', and error states) and must be callable once per client-process lifetime; logout cleanly releases the session.
acceptance_test: Unit test calls login, asserts a healthy session is established, calls it a second time and asserts documented behavior (idempotent or explicit error), then logs out and asserts subsequent calls report no active session.

requirement: A polling function reports whether any parameter has changed since the last check (0 none, 1 new params, negative for no-server), intended to be called on a short interval (documented as 10-20 ms) by clients that don't use push notifications.
acceptance_test: Unit test changes a parameter internally and asserts the dirty flag reports 1 on next poll and 0 thereafter until another change occurs.

requirement: Parameters are addressable by their documented dotted/bracketed name string (e.g. 'Strip[0].Gain') for both get and set as a float value, returning a documented error code for an unknown parameter name or a structural mismatch.
acceptance_test: Property test round-trips get/set for a representative sample of every documented parameter family and asserts correct error codes for a deliberately misspelled parameter name.

requirement: String-valued parameters (e.g. device names, labels, file paths) are gettable/settable via ANSI and wide-character variants, with a documented buffer size limit.
acceptance_test: Unit test round-trips ASCII and UTF-16 strings up to the documented buffer limit and asserts correct truncation/rejection behavior beyond it.

requirement: A single call accepts a multi-statement script (','/ ';' / newline separated, size-limited to the documented 48 KB) applying many parameter changes atomically in source order, returning 0 on success or the 1-based line number of the first error.
acceptance_test: Unit test submits a multi-statement script including one deliberately invalid statement and asserts all valid preceding statements are applied and the correct erroring line number is returned; a script over 48 KB is rejected.

requirement: Both bracket (Strip[i].param) and parenthesis (Strip(i).param) index syntaxes are accepted as equivalent for addressing strip/bus/other indexed families.
acceptance_test: Unit test submits equivalent scripts using bracket and parenthesis syntax and asserts identical resulting state.
