requirement: Parameter assignments support absolute (=), relative-add (+=), and relative-subtract (-=) forms, e.g. Strip(0).gain -=3; applies a -3 dB relative change from the current value, and Strip(0).mute +=1; toggles a boolean.
acceptance_test: Property test applies a sequence of += and -= operations to a numeric parameter and asserts the final value equals the algebraic sum of the deltas from the starting value; applies += to a boolean and asserts it toggles.

requirement: Two-argument function-style parameters (e.g. FadeTo=(dB, ms), FadeBy=(dB, ms)) are parsed as a parenthesized comma-separated tuple attached to the parameter name.
acceptance_test: Unit test parses several documented tuple-valued calls and asserts both arguments are extracted with correct types and range validation.

requirement: Command.* requests are processed before other requests in the same script/packet; a Shutdown command terminates processing of the remainder of the script; a Load command resets/discards any other requests present in the same script.
acceptance_test: Unit test submits a script mixing Command.Load with other parameter assignments and asserts the documented precedence/reset behavior; a script with Command.Shutdown followed by further statements asserts those statements are not applied.

requirement: A level-query function returns pre-fader input, post-fader input, post-mute input, or output peak level in dB for any valid channel index, with documented negative return codes for 'no level available' and 'index out of range'.
acceptance_test: Property test queries all 4 metering points across the full valid channel-index range for the built mixer size and asserts correct values track injected test-tone levels; an out-of-range index returns the documented error code.

requirement: Enumeration functions return a count of available input/output devices and, per index, the device type constant, display name, and hardware id, matching the OS backend's live device list.
acceptance_test: Integration test enumerates devices against the null/mock backend configured with a known device set and asserts count and per-device fields match exactly.

requirement: External clients can register for input, output, or main audio-callback buffers (documented buffer struct with sample rate, frame counts, and up to 128 read/write channel pointers), receive lifecycle commands (STARTING/ENDING/CHANGE), and up to 3 concurrent callback registrations are supported.
acceptance_test: Integration test registers 3 mock callback clients at each of the 3 callback points, drives the engine through start/parameter-change/stop, and asserts each client receives the correct lifecycle commands and buffer contents; a 4th registration attempt is refused if the documented cap is enforced per point.

requirement: A dirty-flag/get/set API surface lets an external client poll for and drive up to 80 logical macro-button states (0.0 OFF / 1.0 ON), including StateOnly, Trigger-enable, and Color-select bit-modes.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets a button's state via SetStatus in each of the 4 documented bitmodes and asserts GetStatus and the dirty flag reflect the change correctly.

requirement: A host application can register a small number of custom on-screen buttons (push or two-position) with a text label, receiving a window-message callback when the button is pressed/released.
acceptance_test: Integration test registers a custom button, simulates a press via the mock UI harness, and asserts the registered callback fires with the documented press/release semantics.

feature: Level and RT channel index maps per mixer size
requirement: Level/RT channel indices are laid out per mixer size (e.g. the 8-strip/8-bus configuration: input channels 0-33 across 5 stereo strips + 3x8-channel virtual strips, output channels 0-63 across 8 buses at fixed 8-channel offsets).
acceptance_test: Unit test asserts the documented input/output channel index ranges and per-strip/per-bus offsets are produced exactly for the 8-strip/8-bus configuration.

requirement: All control-API entry points are documented as thread-safe and non-blocking (aside from explicitly noted exceptions), suitable for calling from a UI or automation thread without stalling it behind the audio thread.
acceptance_test: Property/perf test calls each API entry point concurrently from multiple threads under a fuzzed parameter workload and asserts no data races (via a thread-sanitizer-equivalent check) and bounded per-call latency.

requirement: Option.sr, .ASIOsr, .delay[i], .buffer.mme/.wdm/.ks/.asio, .mode.exclusif, .mode.swift, .MonitorOnSEL, .SliderMode expose the full set of engine-wide configuration options documented in System Settings via the control API, with the ranges specified in their respective feature rows.
acceptance_test: Property test round-trips get/set for every Option.* member at its documented boundary values and asserts the engine-level behavior described in the corresponding devices/dsp-bus rows actually changes.

requirement: patch.asio[i], patch.OutA2..OutA5[i], Patch.composite[j], Patch.insert[k], Patch.PostFaderComposite, Patch.PostFxInsert expose the full documented ASIO/composite/insert routing surface via the control API.
acceptance_test: Property test round-trips get/set for every Patch.* member across its documented index range and asserts the routing behavior described in the corresponding routing/dsp-bus/dsp-strip rows changes accordingly.

requirement: Command.Shutdown/Show/Restart/Reset/Eject/Save/Load/Lock, Command.Button[i].State/StateOnly/Trigger/Color, Command.SaveBUSEQ[j]/LoadBUSEQ[j], Command.SaveStripEQ[j]/LoadStripEQ[j], Command.Preset[k].Recall/Store, Command.RecallPreset/UpdatePreset are all write-only trigger/action parameters, each producing the documented side effect exactly once per invocation.
acceptance_test: Unit test invokes each Command.* action against a mock engine state and asserts the exact documented side effect occurs exactly once, with no effect from a value the action does not recognize.

requirement: netaudio.Enable, netaudio.instream[i].* (on/name/ip/port/sr/channel/bit read-only, quality, route), netaudio.outstream[i].* (on/name/ip/port/sr/channel/bit/quality/route/vfps/vFormat/vQuality/vCursor) for i=0-7 (plus MIDI/FRAME stream slots) expose the full NetAudio configuration surface documented in the netaudio area via the control API.
acceptance_test: Property test round-trips get/set for every netaudio.* member across its documented range/index space and asserts the resulting wire behavior matches the corresponding netaudio-area rows.

requirement: The compatibility shim exposes a queryable version so client wrappers built against an older shim ABI fail fast with a clear error rather than silently misbehaving against a newer/older engine.
acceptance_test: Integration test loads the shim with a client that checks a version function and asserts a deliberately mismatched expected-version check produces a documented, non-crashing error path.

spec_ref: third-party wrapper note in reference doc
requirement: A parameter read immediately following a set on the same client connection returns the newly-set value (no stale-read window across the shim boundary), even though the underlying engine parameter application is asynchronous to the audio thread.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets a parameter and immediately reads it back on the same client and asserts the read reflects the just-written value.

requirement: Macro/script text supports ';', ',' and newline as statement separators and '//' line comments.
acceptance_test: Unit test parses a script using mixed separators and trailing comments and asserts identical resulting statements to an equivalent normalized script.

requirement: Button(i).State (push=1/release=0), Button(i).StateOnly (display-only state change), Button.State (init-script-only, current button), and Button(i).Trigger (enable/disable the audio trigger) are locally interpreted by the macro runner, not sent to the engine as Command.Button (which is reserved for NetAudio-TEXT requests).
acceptance_test: Unit test invokes each local Button(i).* instruction from within a button script and asserts the documented local effect, and that Command.Button issued locally (not via NetAudio-TEXT) is rejected/ignored per the documented warning.

requirement: Wait(ms) introduces a timed pause between subsequent statements within a script.
acceptance_test: Unit test issues two statements separated by Wait(200) and asserts the second statement's effect is observed at least 200ms after the first, using a controllable test clock.

requirement: Load("filename") loads a different button map file, replacing the currently active set of macro buttons.
acceptance_test: Integration test triggers Load() to a second button map file and asserts the active button set switches to the loaded map's definitions.

requirement: Show(0) hides and Show(1) shows the macro-buttons application window from within a script.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test triggers Show(0) then Show(1) and asserts the window visibility toggles accordingly.

requirement: SendMidi(target, type, ...) (optionally prefixed System.) sends note-on, note-off, ctrl-change, prg-change (channels 1-16, decimal values), or raw hex 'data' byte sequences to a named MIDI output target (a physical MIDI-out device or a NetAudio-MIDI stream name).
acceptance_test: Unit test invokes SendMidi for each of the 4 typed message kinds plus a raw-data call and asserts the exact resulting MIDI bytes match the documented encoding for each; both the System.-prefixed and bare forms parse identically.

requirement: SendText(streamName, script) sends an arbitrary multi-statement control-API script to a named outgoing NetAudio-TEXT stream in one call (supporting embedded newlines, closing at the matching final parenthesis); BEGIN_SECTION(streamName) ... END_SECTION achieves the same for a block of statements.
acceptance_test: Unit test uses both SendText and BEGIN_SECTION/END_SECTION forms to dispatch an equivalent multi-statement script and asserts the mock NetAudio-TEXT stream receives byte-identical resulting scripts.

requirement: System.KeyDown/KeyUp/KeyPress accept a combination string of 1-4 keys (e.g. "CTRL+SHIFT+F10") from a documented key-name table (letters/digits, navigation, numpad, media/browser keys, modifiers, F1-F24) and simulate the corresponding OS key event(s); KeyPress issues Down then Up.
acceptance_test: E2E test issues KeyDown/KeyUp/KeyPress for representative simple and combination key strings against a mock input-injection target and asserts the correct OS key events are synthesized in the correct order.

requirement: System.SetFocus(appName) attempts to bring a named application window to keyboard focus; System.ResetFocus() restores prior focus.
acceptance_test: E2E test with two mock windows invokes SetFocus and asserts the target window becomes focused, then ResetFocus and asserts the original window regains focus.

requirement: System.Mouse(action) synthesizes a left/right/middle mouse button down/up event at the current cursor position.
acceptance_test: E2E test invokes each of the 6 documented mouse actions and asserts the corresponding synthesized OS mouse event.

requirement: System.Execute(program, workdir, args) launches an external process (with %envname% environment-variable substitution and %% / %' escaping) either waiting for completion (/K-style) or firing-and-forgetting (/C-style) per the documented shell semantics.
acceptance_test: Integration test invokes System.Execute with an environment-variable reference in the arguments and asserts correct substitution and that the target process is launched with the documented working directory.

requirement: System.DMXSetValue(address, channel, value[, value2, ...]) stages one or more DMX512 channel values and System.DMXCommit() sends the staged frame over a configured serial DMX interface.
acceptance_test: Integration test stages several channel values and commits, and asserts a mock DMX serial interface receives a correctly-framed DMX512 packet with the documented channel/value mapping.

requirement: SendMidi/System.SendMidi accept a NetAudio outgoing-stream name (e.g. "netaudio1") as an alternate target alongside physical MIDI-out device names, transparently choosing the NetAudio-MIDI wire path.
acceptance_test: Unit test targets SendMidi at a NetAudio stream name and asserts the message is serialized onto the NetAudio-MIDI SERIAL sub-protocol rather than a physical MIDI device.

feature: Macro button count and index range
requirement: The macro application supports 4 to 80 buttons, addressed by a zero-based logical index 0-79 in both the local app and the control API.
acceptance_test: Unit test creates buttons at index 0 and 79 and asserts both are individually addressable via get/set status; index 80 is rejected.

requirement: Each button is configured as Push (momentary: ON while held/clicked, OFF on release, triggering the ON/OFF scripts respectively) or 2 Positions (latching toggle between two states).
acceptance_test: E2E test creates one Push and one 2-Positions button and asserts the documented state-transition and script-firing behavior for each type under click/release simulation.

requirement: Each button stores three independent scripts: an initial-condition script (sent once at application startup), a push script, and a release script.
acceptance_test: Unit test configures distinct scripts for init/push/release, starts the app, and asserts the init script fires once at startup, the push script fires on press, and the release script fires on release.

feature: Keyboard shortcut trigger with Exclusive Key
requirement: A button can be bound to a keyboard shortcut chosen from a documented key/mouse combination list, with an 'Exclusive Key' option that reserves the key so it is not simultaneously forwarded to other applications.
acceptance_test: E2E test binds a shortcut with Exclusive Key enabled, simulates the key combo, and asserts the button fires and the key event is not observed by a background mock application; without Exclusive Key the event is also forwarded.

requirement: A button can be bound to a MIDI event learned from the MIDI Mapping dialog's input device(s) or from an incoming NetAudio-MIDI stream, with LEARN/RESET actions.
acceptance_test: Integration test learns a MIDI CC as a button trigger, sends the matching MIDI message, and asserts the button fires; RESET clears the binding.

requirement: A button can be bound to a control on up to 4 connected XInput gamepads.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates an XInput button press on gamepad index 0-3 mapped to a macro button and asserts the button fires.

feature: Audio-level trigger with IN/OUT thresholds and Hold
requirement: A button can be driven by an input strip or output bus level crossing an IN threshold (pushes the button) and releasing when it drops below an OUT threshold, with a minimum Hold time keeping the button pushed, measured pre-fader, post-fader, or post-mute per a selectable mode.
acceptance_test: Integration test drives a synthetic signal above the IN threshold on a strip configured for each of the 3 measurement modes and asserts the button pushes; drops the signal below OUT and asserts release only after the Hold time elapses.

requirement: A generic HID device/control (including otherwise-unmappable keyboard/mouse controls) can be bound to a button via a Learn-enabled HID Manager dialog.
acceptance_test: Integration test learns a synthetic HID input event as a button trigger and asserts the button responds to that exact HID event thereafter.

requirement: A button can be bound to one of 16 general-purpose digital inputs on an external USB GPIO module (2 banks of 8 via two DB9 connectors), for foot pedals / physical switches.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates a GPIO input transition on a mock GPIO backend mapped to a button and asserts the button fires correspondingly.

requirement: A button's background can be set to one of 9 documented color options (0-8), addressable both from the button-configuration dialog and remotely via Command.Button[i].Color.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets each of the 9 color values via the remote command and asserts the button's rendered/stored color state matches.

requirement: Each button has independently editable name and sub-name text fields displayed on the button face.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets name and sub-name and asserts both render on the button and persist across save/load.

requirement: A button can display separate custom images for its OFF and ON states, loaded from BMP/PNG/JPG/TIF files; images at the native 130x108 px size are shown as-is, larger images are reframed/scaled, smaller images are centered, and transparency (with shadow) is honored only for PNG images smaller than the native size; when an image is set, the keyboard-shortcut label is hidden.
acceptance_test: Unit test loads an OFF-state and ON-state image of the native size, a larger size, and a smaller transparent PNG, and asserts the documented scale/center/transparency handling for each case; asserts the shortcut label is suppressed once an image is set.

requirement: A button's displayed/latched state can be driven by an engine transport event (tape PLAY, STOP, REC, or End-Of-File) rather than a local input device.
acceptance_test: Integration test binds a button to each of the 4 documented transport events and asserts the button's state changes at the corresponding transport transition.

spec_ref: PM p.64; forum note on system-menu Copy/Paste/Load/Save
requirement: The complete set of button configurations (scripts, triggers, images, colors) can be saved to and loaded from a file, and individual button configurations can be copied and pasted between buttons.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures several buttons, copies one configuration onto another, saves the map, reloads it in a fresh instance, and asserts every button's configuration is restored exactly.

requirement: An option launches the macro/automation application automatically whenever the main engine/UI process starts.
acceptance_test: Integration test enables the option, restarts the engine process, and asserts the macro application process is started automatically.

spec_ref: Decision spine architecture #6; PM p.44-47 (fixed-size defect)
requirement: The main mixer window is freely resizable and renders crisply at any OS display-scaling factor (100%-300%), unlike the incumbent's fixed-pixel bitmap-drawn layout.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test renders the main window at 100%, 150%, 200%, and 300% OS scale and asserts no clipped/overlapping controls and no blurred/pixelated raster artifacts via a screenshot-diff baseline per scale factor.

requirement: The UI supports at minimum light and dark themes, switchable at runtime without restart, with all custom controls (knobs, faders, meters) themed consistently.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test switches theme at runtime and asserts a screenshot-diff baseline for both themes shows correct, consistent color application with no unthemed default-OS-widget artifacts.

requirement: Every interactive control exposes a correct accessibility role, name, and current value via the platform accessibility tree, and is keyboard-navigable without a mouse.
acceptance_test: Automated a11y-tree test walks every visible control after each major dialog opens and asserts each has a non-empty accessible name/role and that Tab-order keyboard navigation reaches every interactive control.

feature: UI process separated from engine, testable via protocol
requirement: The UI runs as a separate OS process from the audio engine, communicating exclusively over the canonical control protocol, and can be driven/tested by scripting the same protocol plus screenshot/a11y-tree assertions.
acceptance_test: Integration test launches the UI process pointed at a headless engine instance (null backend), drives a full user workflow purely via control-protocol messages, and asserts the UI reflects the resulting state via screenshot/a11y-tree checks.

requirement: The main menu exposes Restart Audio Engine, auto-restart-on-A1-disconnect, auto-restart-on-any-disconnect, and Shutdown actions, each mapped 1:1 to the corresponding Command.* control-API call.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test invokes each menu item and asserts the corresponding Command.* action is issued and its documented effect occurs.

requirement: The main menu exposes Load Settings, Save Settings, Load Settings on Startup, and Reset Settings actions, each mapped to the corresponding Command.Load/Save/Reset control-API call plus a startup-file preference.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test invokes Save then Reset then Load and asserts the exact prior state is restored; asserts a configured startup file is auto-loaded on next launch.

requirement: The main menu exposes System Tray, Run on OS Startup, Show App on Startup, Always Visible (on top), and Lock GUI toggles.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test toggles each option and asserts the corresponding OS-level behavior (tray presence, autostart registration, initial visibility, always-on-top, input-lock) is applied.

requirement: An option binds the OS media volume keys to control the level of bus A1, bus A2, or strip 1 (input 1), selectable, and a documented mute hotkey mutes the corresponding target.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test enables the hook targeting bus A2, presses the OS volume-up key, and asserts bus A2's gain increases; the mute hotkey mutes the corresponding target.

feature: Main menu: Limit Remote Gain to 0dB
requirement: A menu toggle caps MIDI/remote-driven gain changes at 0 dB instead of the full +12 dB ceiling (see dsp-strip row for the underlying behavior).
acceptance_test: E2E UI test toggles the menu item and asserts the underlying Option is set/cleared and the corresponding clamp behavior activates.

feature: Main menu: contextual help in caption
requirement: A default-on option shows context-sensitive help text (naming the equivalent control-API instruction) in the window caption/status area based on current mouse-hover target.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test hovers over a known control and asserts the caption/status area shows the expected help text including the matching control-API parameter name.

requirement: The main menu launches System Settings, Recording Options, MIDI Mapping, and NetAudio configuration dialogs.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test invokes each menu item and asserts the corresponding dialog opens and is populated with live engine state.

requirement: Documented global shortcuts are implemented: double-click any control resets it to default; a modifier+click opens a precision entry slider; a modifier+right-click opens a value-entry box or triggers undo on detail-parameter knobs; a documented chord opens the main menu; a documented chord restarts the engine.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test exercises each documented shortcut on a representative control and asserts the exact documented behavior (reset-to-default, precision slider, value-entry box, undo, menu-open, engine-restart).

requirement: Right-clicking a strip or bus header opens a menu offering Reset/Copy/Paste/Save/Load for the whole strip/bus or for each of its DSP sub-sections independently (EQ, pan panel, dynamics, denoiser/pitch, FX sends).
acceptance_test: E2E UI test uses the per-section Copy action on one strip's EQ only and Paste onto another strip, then asserts only the EQ state (not gain/dynamics/etc.) was transferred.

requirement: Right-clicking (or an equivalent gesture on) a strip/bus fader's bottom area opens an inline or dialog text editor to set its Label, shown vertically inside the fader trough thereafter.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test renames a strip and asserts the new label displays in the fader trough and is retrievable via Strip[i].Label.

feature: Simplified resizable remote view (Streamer View equivalent)
requirement: A separate, resizable, simplified view shows only labeled strips/buses with essential controls (mute, gain, MON) for at-a-glance/streaming use, driven over the same control protocol as the main UI.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test opens the simplified view alongside the main UI, changes a control in one, and asserts the other reflects the change live.

requirement: A resizable preset-browser window lists a bank of stored full-mixer-state presets (excluding device selection/system settings/MIDI/NetAudio), recallable by click/Enter or the first N presets via function-key hotkeys.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test stores 3 presets, recalls one by hotkey and one by click, and asserts the exact stored strip/bus parameter state (but not device selection) is restored each time.

requirement: Contextual help text is stored in an external, swappable data file (not hard-coded in the binary), enabling future localization without a rebuild.
acceptance_test: Unit test swaps the help-text data file for an alternate-language version and asserts the UI's contextual help displays the alternate text without a rebuild.

requirement: The complete mixer configuration (routing, strip/bus parameters, options, patch, NetAudio, MIDI map) round-trips through a single structured, human-readable file format (e.g. TOML/JSON, replacing the incumbent's ad hoc XML) loadable by Load Settings and writable by Save Settings.
acceptance_test: Integration test saves settings, mutates state, loads settings back, and asserts every documented parameter family round-trips exactly; a hand-edited file with one invalid field produces a clear, non-crashing validation error naming the offending field.

feature: Settings versioning and daily backup copies
requirement: Each settings save records a schema version, and the settings store keeps at least two automatic rolling backups (equivalent to the incumbent's 'today'/'yesterday' copies) so a corrupted or unwanted save can be recovered.
acceptance_test: Integration test saves settings on two different simulated days and asserts both a current and a previous-day backup are retrievable and independently loadable.

requirement: A 64-slot preset bank stores full mixer parameter state (excluding device selection, system settings, MIDI map, and NetAudio configuration) recallable individually, with the first 24 addressable via function-key hotkeys.
acceptance_test: Integration test stores distinct state into all 64 preset slots, recalls a sample of them (including one via an F-key equivalent call), and asserts recalled state matches exactly and excluded categories (devices/options/MIDI/NetAudio) are left untouched.

requirement: The application binary accepts documented command-line flags: hide-GUI, restart-engine, and load-a-named-settings-file-at-startup, matching the incumbent's -h/-R/-l"file" contract for scripted deployment.
acceptance_test: Integration test launches the binary with each flag and asserts the documented behavior (hidden window, engine restart triggered, named settings file loaded) occurs.

requirement: Advanced/expert options equivalent to the incumbent's registry keys (engine start delay, preferred bit resolution, monitoring-delay ceiling, pre-recording buffer max, system timer resolution, auto-up-mix mode, engine-mode bit flags) are exposed in one documented, discoverable configuration surface rather than an undocumented registry-only path.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets each expert option via the documented config surface and asserts the corresponding engine behavior (validated in its own feature-area row) responds; the config surface round-trips through the human-readable settings file.

requirement: A diagnostics view lists all installed OPENMIX virtual devices/drivers per platform and flags any missing or duplicated entry versus the expected set for the current build.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates a missing virtual device on the null backend's mock device registry and asserts the diagnostics view flags exactly that device as missing.

requirement: The Windows host-I/O backend implements the shared host-I/O trait using WASAPI (shared and exclusive), Kernel Streaming, and optionally ASIO (only with a locally supplied SDK).
acceptance_test: Integration test exercises device enumeration, open, buffer callback, and close against real or virtual WASAPI/KS devices on a Windows CI runner.

requirement: The macOS host-I/O backend implements the shared host-I/O trait using CoreAudio (AudioUnit/HAL).
acceptance_test: Integration test exercises device enumeration, open, buffer callback, and close against CoreAudio devices on a macOS CI runner.

requirement: The Linux host-I/O backend implements the shared host-I/O trait using PipeWire (preferred) with an ALSA fallback.
acceptance_test: Integration test exercises device enumeration, open, buffer callback, and close against PipeWire and ALSA devices on a Linux CI runner.

requirement: A signed Windows kernel-mode virtual-audio driver exposes engine strips/buses as OS playback/recording endpoints; this workstream is isolated from the rest of the build so the mixer ships and is fully testable without it.
acceptance_test: CI asserts the full engine/DSP/control-API/UI test suite builds, runs, and passes with the kernel-driver feature entirely disabled/absent; a separate, gated driver test suite runs only where a signed test driver is installable.

requirement: A macOS HAL (Halide/AudioServerPlugin) plug-in exposes engine strips/buses as OS playback/recording endpoints.
acceptance_test: Integration test installs the HAL plug-in in a macOS CI runner, plays audio into a virtual endpoint, and asserts it is captured on the corresponding engine strip.

requirement: PipeWire virtual source/sink nodes expose engine strips/buses as OS-visible endpoints on Linux without requiring a kernel module.
acceptance_test: Integration test creates PipeWire virtual nodes on a Linux CI runner, routes audio through them, and asserts correct engine strip/bus capture and playback.

requirement: The null/loopback backend implements the full host-I/O and virtual-device traits (deterministic silence/loopback generation) so every engine-level test can run identically on any CI platform without real audio hardware.
acceptance_test: CI test runs the complete cross-platform test suite against only the null backend on Linux, macOS, and Windows runners and asserts identical pass/fail results across all three.

requirement: Continuous integration builds and runs the null-backend test suite on Linux, macOS, and Windows on every change, gating merges on all three passing.
acceptance_test: CI pipeline configuration is asserted (by a meta-test) to include Linux/macOS/Windows build+test jobs on the null backend and to block merge on any job failing.

feature: No credential/secret leakage in control-API shim
requirement: The compatibility ABI shim and canonical control protocol never require or transmit OS credentials, and any local IPC channel used between UI and engine is restricted to the local user by OS-appropriate access control.
acceptance_test: Security review checks the IPC/socket permissions the engine listens on and asserts only the invoking OS user (not other local users) can connect; a fuzz test targets the shim's parameter-name parser for buffer-safety issues.

requirement: Because NetAudio-TEXT accepts arbitrary control-API scripts from any source address with no authentication, the engine validates and bounds every parsed statement (index ranges, string lengths, numeric ranges) so a malicious or malformed script cannot corrupt engine state or crash the process.
acceptance_test: Fuzz test feeds malformed/adversarial NetAudio-TEXT scripts (oversized indices, huge strings, malformed tuples, embedded control characters) at the parser for an extended run and asserts no crash, no memory-safety violation, and no out-of-range state mutation.

requirement: All NetAudio header and sub-protocol parsers (AUDIO/SERIAL/TXT/FRAME/SERVICE) reject malformed or truncated packets safely without panics, unbounded memory growth, or undefined behavior, since any host on the network can send arbitrary UDP to the listening port.
acceptance_test: Continuous fuzz target runs the full packet-parsing pipeline against random and structure-aware inputs and asserts no crash/panic/UB/OOM across a large iteration budget, integrated into CI as a fuzz regression corpus.

requirement: The optional 'sync' network transport (used for multi-room/VPN scenarios) supports authenticated encryption of the audio/control payload, so streams need not rely solely on network-level trust (addressing the incumbent's documented lack of any NetAudio encryption/authentication).
acceptance_test: Interop test establishes a sync-transport session between two engine instances with encryption enabled, captures the wire traffic, and asserts payload bytes are not recoverable as plaintext audio/control data without the negotiated key; a tampered ciphertext packet is rejected rather than applied.

requirement: The Windows kernel-mode virtual-device driver is built and signed through a documented, reproducible signing pipeline compatible with current Windows driver-signing and Secure Boot requirements.
acceptance_test: Manual release-checklist test installs the signed driver package on a clean Windows VM with Secure Boot and HVCI/Memory-Integrity enabled and asserts installation succeeds with no signature-trust warnings.

spec_ref: Decision spine (implied by removing incumbent nags/telemetry concerns)
requirement: The application makes no outbound network calls (license checks, telemetry, update pings) unless the user has explicitly enabled a specific opt-in feature (e.g. update check), addressing the incumbent's activation-server contact and ecosystem privacy concerns.
acceptance_test: Integration test runs the application with network access blocked at the OS firewall level and asserts full core functionality (mixing, routing, recording, local control API) works with zero outbound connection attempts observed, except for explicitly user-enabled features.

requirement: A plain (unencrypted, unauthenticated) audio-streaming mode is wire-compatible with the incumbent's/VBAN-family NetAudio protocol (header, sub-protocols, sample-rate table, packet limits as documented in the netaudio area) so existing third-party NetAudio senders/receivers interoperate without modification.
acceptance_test: Interop test streams audio between OPENMIX and at least one independent third-party VBAN/NetAudio-compatible implementation (e.g. an open-source receiver/emitter) in both directions and asserts correct audio transfer.

requirement: The optional sync transport tags each packet with a sender-clock timestamp so receivers can align multiple streams (e.g. multi-room speaker groups) more tightly than the plain protocol's clock-free model allows.
acceptance_test: Integration test streams the same source to two sync-transport receivers over simulated differing network paths and asserts their playback timing converges within a documented tight tolerance (materially better than the plain-protocol baseline), using the embedded timestamps for alignment.

feature: Sync transport: optional forward error correction
requirement: The sync transport optionally applies forward error correction to recover from a bounded rate of packet loss without requiring retransmission, trading bandwidth for resilience on lossy Wi-Fi/VPN links.
acceptance_test: Integration test injects a configured packet-loss rate under FEC enabled vs disabled and asserts audio is recovered without audible dropout up to the FEC's documented correctable-loss threshold, and gracefully degrades beyond it.

requirement: The sync transport can be run in an authenticated-encryption mode end-to-end between a specific sender/receiver pair, distinct from the plain interop mode, for use over untrusted networks/VPNs.
acceptance_test: See security area's encrypted-transport row for the acceptance test; this row tracks the network-ext feature flag that selects sync-mode-with-encryption versus plain VBAN-compatible mode at stream-configuration time.

requirement: A named group of sync-transport receivers can be targeted by one logical source stream (fan-out), with each group member independently reporting its own sync/quality status back to the sender.
acceptance_test: Integration test creates a 3-receiver group, streams to it, and asserts all 3 receivers play in tight sync per the sync-transport timing test, and that each receiver's individually reported status (quality/error counters) is retrievable at the sender.

requirement: An optional network clock-synchronization mechanism (e.g. PTP-like exchange over the sync transport) lets multiple engine instances agree on a shared time base for tighter multi-room alignment than timestamp-only sync alone.
acceptance_test: Integration test enables clock-sync between two engine instances on simulated independent hardware clocks with a known drift and asserts their reported clock offset converges to near zero and stream alignment improves versus clock-sync disabled.

spec_ref: PM p.55 (error LED taxonomy, see netaudio area)
requirement: The sync transport reports the same class of per-stream health telemetry (loss/reorder/corruption/underrun-equivalent counters) as the plain-protocol error-LED set, for parity of diagnosability between the two transports.
acceptance_test: Unit test injects loss/reorder/corruption conditions on the sync transport and asserts each produces a distinctly countable telemetry event, mirroring the plain-protocol error taxonomy test.

requirement: The mixer ships native builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux (not Windows-only), with NetAudio interop available as sender and receiver on all three, fixing the incumbent's Windows-only architecture.
acceptance_test: Integration test builds and runs the full engine/DSP/control-API test suite natively on Linux, macOS, and Windows CI runners.

feature: Robust behavior across OS feature/driver updates
requirement: Virtual-device driver/plug-in updates are tested against current OS feature-update previews as part of release gating, and the engine degrades gracefully (falls back to non-virtual-device operation) rather than blocking the OS update or blue-screening if a driver incompatibility is detected, fixing the incumbent's Windows-11-24H2 BSOD/update-block history.
acceptance_test: Manual release-checklist test installs the current driver on the latest available OS preview/insider build and asserts no BSOD/kernel panic occurs and the OS update is not blocked; an integration test asserts the engine falls back to host-I/O-only mode if virtual-device registration fails at startup.

requirement: Installing, uninstalling, and updating the application (including its virtual-device components where the OS allows) does not require a mandatory reboot after each operation, fixing the incumbent's two-reboot update procedure.
acceptance_test: Integration test performs install, then update-in-place, then uninstall on a clean VM and asserts the application is fully functional/removed after each step without an intervening reboot, on platforms where the OS driver model allows it; where a reboot is unavoidable (documented OS constraint), the installer clearly states so and batches it to a single reboot.

feature: Driver install/signing that avoids AV/security-tool false positives
requirement: The virtual-device driver installer is signed and structured to minimize behavior patterns (e.g. unexplained driver drops, trust-setting checks) that commonly trigger antivirus/EDR false-positive flags, and ships a documented allow-listing guide.
acceptance_test: Manual test submits the release installer to at least one reputable multi-engine AV scanning service and asserts a clean or near-clean result, with any remaining flags documented and explained in release notes.

feature: Stable audio callback (no crackle/underrun) across common configs
requirement: The engine avoids crackle/underrun/glitch artifacts under the documented common failure conditions (undersized buffer for the device, same physical device opened twice, sample-rate mismatch downstream, background CPU contention) either by validating configuration up front or by graceful automatic recovery.
acceptance_test: Integration/perf test runs a battery of the documented problem configurations (tiny buffer, duplicate device open attempt, mismatched downstream sample rate, injected CPU load) and asserts either the configuration is rejected/corrected with a clear message, or audio continues glitch-free per a defined objective glitch-detection metric.

requirement: End-to-end latency for each backend class (ASIO/WASAPI-exclusive/WASAPI-shared/PipeWire/CoreAudio) at each supported buffer size is measured, documented, and regression-tested, replacing the incumbent's inconsistent/undocumented latency figures.
acceptance_test: Perf test measures round-trip loopback latency for each backend class at its minimum supported buffer size and asserts it stays within a documented target band, failing CI on regression beyond a set tolerance.

requirement: When a previously-selected audio device is unplugged and later replugged (or a Bluetooth/wireless device drops and reconnects), the engine automatically detects the reconnection and resumes streaming to/from it without requiring a manual engine restart.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates unplug then replug of a mock device on the null backend's device-notification hook and asserts the engine automatically resumes streaming without any external restart command, within a documented reconnect-latency budget.

feature: ASIO channel/device flexibility beyond a single A1 device
requirement: Buses and strips can reach ASIO hardware channels through a documented, validated patch/routing model (as in the incumbent) but with clearer validation and error messages for overlapping-channel misconfiguration, and the design leaves room for a future multi-ASIO-device mode without a major rework.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures an overlapping-channel ASIO patch as in the routing-area test and asserts a clear warning/diagnostic is surfaced (not just silent overwrite) identifying the conflicting bus assignments.

requirement: The engine can host CLAP audio-effect plug-ins on strip insert points and bus FX sends/returns as an alternative or supplement to the built-in EQ/dynamics/reverb/delay, addressing the incumbent's lack of any native plug-in hosting.
acceptance_test: Integration test loads a reference open-source CLAP plug-in onto a strip insert point, processes a known test signal through it, and asserts the plug-in's documented effect is audible/measurable in the engine's output, with graceful handling of a plug-in that crashes or reports an incompatible format.
notes: Decision spine explicitly designates CLAP hosting as a later milestone (M7), not required for the initial Max-parity build.

requirement: Advanced/expert configuration is organized behind clearly labeled 'advanced' panels with inline documentation, and the default/simple view exposes only commonly-needed controls, reducing the incumbent's documented steep learning curve and registry-only expert options.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test asserts the default view's control count is below a documented ceiling and that every advanced-only control is reachable through one clearly labeled disclosure action, with inline help text present for each.

feature: Resizable, DPI-aware, themeable UI (no fixed pixel layout)
requirement: The main window and all dialogs are resizable, DPI-aware at any OS scaling factor, and themeable (light/dark), fixing the incumbent's fixed-pixel bitmap GUI that does not scale on high-DPI/4K displays.
acceptance_test: See the ui-area 'Resizable, DPI-aware main window' and 'Themeable UI' rows for the concrete acceptance tests; this row tracks the defect-catalogue requirement these two UI rows jointly satisfy.

feature: Bounded, documented CPU/RAM/GPU footprint while idle
requirement: The idle (no active audio processing beyond silence) CPU, RAM, and GPU footprint of the engine and UI process combined stays within a documented budget on reference hardware, and never engages GPU acceleration unless a feature that needs it (e.g. video screen-share) is active.
acceptance_test: Perf test measures idle CPU/RAM/GPU usage on reference hardware over a sustained period and asserts it stays within the documented budget, and that GPU usage is zero when no GPU-requiring feature is enabled.

feature: Correct exclusive/shared mode negotiation and fallback
requirement: When a requested exclusive-mode device open fails (already in use, or exclusive access disabled by the OS), the engine automatically and silently falls back to shared mode and surfaces a clear, non-blocking notification rather than failing to produce audio.
acceptance_test: Integration test forces an exclusive-open failure on a mock device and asserts the engine falls back to shared mode automatically and a non-blocking notification event is emitted.

requirement: Applications that ignore explicit device selection and rely on the OS default device are handled via a documented, discoverable 'set OPENMIX as default' workflow with an in-app checklist verifying default playback/recording/communications role assignment, reducing the incumbent's default-device-hijack confusion.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test runs the in-app default-device checklist against a mock OS device-role API and asserts it correctly reports and can remediate a mismatched default-device configuration.

requirement: The application exposes and, where the OS allows, sets the 'do not duck other applications' communications-device policy automatically for its own virtual endpoints when they are used with VoIP applications, rather than requiring the user to find and change a buried OS setting.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets a virtual endpoint as the OS communications device and asserts the ducking policy is set to 'do nothing' automatically (or the user is clearly prompted) rather than silently ducking other streams.

feature: Documented Bluetooth profile guidance and reconnect resilience
requirement: Bluetooth device profile limitations (A2DP-vs-HFP mic/quality tradeoff) are surfaced with in-app guidance at device-selection time, and Bluetooth device disconnect/reconnect is covered by the same automatic-reconnect requirement as wired hot-plug.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test selects a mock Bluetooth device and asserts an in-app advisory about the A2DP/HFP tradeoff is shown; integration test covers reconnect via the same test as the auto-reconnect defect-fix row.

feature: No known anti-cheat interference by design
requirement: The engine avoids driver/hooking techniques known to trigger anti-cheat kernel-integrity checks beyond what is strictly necessary for the virtual-device driver, and this risk is documented and monitored as part of release testing.
acceptance_test: Manual test runs the application alongside a representative set of anti-cheat-protected titles in a documented compatibility test pass before each release and records any detected interference.

requirement: The application detects a likely sample-rate mismatch for known common downstream consumers (e.g. a virtual endpoint feeding a communications app that prefers 48 kHz) and proactively suggests the correct setting rather than requiring the user to discover it via forum posts.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures a virtual endpoint at a non-48kHz format while a mock 'prefers 48kHz' consumer is attached and asserts a proactive suggestion/notification is surfaced.

feature: No unencrypted, unauthenticated network audio by default off-LAN
requirement: Plain NetAudio-compatible streaming remains available for LAN interop (see network-ext area), but the sync transport with encryption is the recommended and easily selectable default for any stream configured to leave the local network (e.g. targeting a non-private IP range), reducing the incumbent's documented no-encryption/no-auth exposure.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures an outgoing stream to a public (non-RFC1918/ULA) destination address and asserts the UI/API surfaces a clear prompt or default recommendation to use the encrypted sync transport instead of the plain protocol.

requirement: Recording is not artificially capped at 2 GiB for common formats (the engine either uses a 64-bit-size-capable container by default or seamlessly spans files at the boundary) and multichannel MP3-equivalent lossy recording is supported via a modern codec (e.g. multichannel Opus/AAC) alongside the legacy stereo-only MP3 option.
acceptance_test: Integration test drives a synthetic recording past 2 GiB in the default format and asserts no interruption/corruption occurs (either via 64-bit size support or seamless file-spanning); a multichannel lossy-codec recording test asserts more than 2 channels encode correctly.

spec_ref: Part 2 Disadvantages catalogue §20; Decision spine (implied automation improvement)
requirement: The macro/automation scripting layer supports basic conditionals (if/else), comparison operators, and simple user-defined variables, in addition to the incumbent's linear Wait/Button/SendMidi/SendText model, so common automation patterns do not require an external scripting language.
acceptance_test: Unit test writes a macro script using an if/else branch on a variable holding a mixer level query result and asserts the correct branch executes based on the runtime value.

requirement: In addition to the compatibility dirty-flag/poll model, the canonical control protocol supports push notification of parameter changes and level updates to subscribed clients, avoiding the incumbent's mandatory 10-20ms polling loop for responsive UIs.
acceptance_test: Integration test subscribes a client to push notifications for a parameter, changes it, and asserts the client receives a notification within a documented low latency without polling.

requirement: The application never displays a purchase/activation nag dialog and performs no license-check network calls, since OPENMIX ships without the incumbent's donationware activation-nag mechanism.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test runs the application continuously across a simulated 40-day period and asserts no nag/activation dialog ever appears and no license-related network call is attempted.

feature: Single-maintainer continuity risk mitigated by open contribution model
spec_ref: Part 2 Disadvantages catalogue §23; Decision spine (two-agent + OSS framing)
requirement: The project's build, test, and contribution process (open engine core, documented protocol, CI-gated PRs from either coding agent) is structured so no single unavailable contributor blocks a critical OS-compatibility fix from shipping.
acceptance_test: Meta/process test (CI configuration check) asserts the contribution pipeline requires only automated CI gating (no single human/agent approval bottleneck hard-coded) to merge a passing, reviewed fix.

feature: PCM-only signal path documented and tested (no bitstream passthrough claims)
requirement: The engine explicitly documents and tests that it processes PCM only and does not claim or attempt Dolby/DTS/Atmos bitstream passthrough, avoiding the incumbent's documented confusion around 'Atmos via PCM.'
acceptance_test: Unit test feeds a non-PCM bitstream-formatted buffer at the engine's input and asserts it is either explicitly rejected with a clear diagnostic or documented as unsupported, rather than silently mis-decoded.

requirement: The engine documents and enforces one explicit channel-order convention (matching the SMPTE/WAV-extensible L,R,C,LFE,RL,RR,SL,SR-style order used throughout this matrix) for all multichannel virtual-strip and bus-mode processing, with conversion tables for OS-default orders that differ.
acceptance_test: Property test asserts every bus-mode formula and virtual-strip channel operation is applied against the documented fixed channel order, and a conversion utility correctly remaps to/from a differing OS-default order in an interop test.

requirement: The sample-rate-converter used whenever a device or stream runs at a rate other than the engine's master rate meets a documented minimum quality bar (e.g. a measurable THD+N / aliasing-rejection threshold), unlike the incumbent's unpublished SRC quality.
acceptance_test: Golden/perf test measures the SRC's THD+N and aliasing rejection on a standard test signal set (e.g. multitone, sweep) at representative rate-conversion ratios and asserts the results meet the documented minimum quality bar.

feature: Engine recovers cleanly when no device is ready at boot
requirement: If no configured device is available/ready when the engine attempts to start, the engine falls back to the internal-clock mode (see engine-area row) rather than remaining in a stuck/unusable state, and a subsequent device-available event is picked up automatically per the auto-reconnect requirement.
acceptance_test: Integration test starts the engine with zero available devices and asserts it comes up in internal-clock mode rather than a failed/hung state; when a device later becomes available, asserts it is picked up automatically.

feature: No conflicts assumed with other audio-enhancement drivers by design
requirement: The engine's device-opening strategy (shared-mode-first negotiation, no assumption of exclusive hardware ownership) is designed and tested to coexist with other third-party audio-enhancement software sharing the same physical device where the OS permits concurrent access.
acceptance_test: Integration test opens a mock device concurrently from OPENMIX and a second mock 'enhancement' consumer in shared mode and asserts both continue operating without one crashing or silently losing audio.

requirement: An unhandled fault in a non-critical engine subsystem (e.g. a single insert/plug-in host) is isolated and does not take down the entire audio engine process; the process supervisor can automatically restart a crashed engine and resume the last-known-good configuration.
acceptance_test: Integration test deliberately crashes a sandboxed subsystem (e.g. a mock faulty plug-in host) and asserts the rest of the engine keeps processing audio; a full-process-crash test asserts a supervisor restarts the engine and reloads the last saved/auto-saved state.

feature: Undo/redo for parameter and routing changes
requirement: A multi-level undo/redo stack covers user-initiated parameter and routing changes made through the UI, addressing the incumbent's complete lack of undo beyond a per-control double-click reset.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test performs a sequence of distinct parameter/routing changes, invokes undo multiple times, and asserts state steps back exactly through the sequence; redo restores forward through the same sequence.

requirement: Per-application volume/mute control for applications routed through a virtual strip is a first-class, reliably-refreshing feature (not dependent on a manual 'restart audio engine' workaround when the OS app list goes stale).
acceptance_test: Integration test opens and closes several mock application audio sessions on a virtual strip in sequence and asserts the per-app control list updates automatically and correctly without requiring any manual refresh/restart action.

feature: No unsolicited telemetry; documented privacy stance with verification
requirement: The application's 'no data collection' privacy claim is independently verifiable: an automated test asserts no outbound network traffic occurs during normal operation except for features the user has explicitly enabled (see security-area row for the concrete test).
acceptance_test: See the security-area 'No telemetry without explicit opt-in' row for the acceptance test; this row tracks the Part-2-defect-catalogue requirement that motivates it.

feature: Documented single-instance and multi-tier switching behavior
requirement: The application's single-instance-per-machine behavior (if retained) and any tiered feature-set switching (equivalent to the incumbent's Standard/Plus/Max) are explicitly documented and tested, rather than left as unverified forum folklore.
acceptance_test: Integration test attempts to launch a second instance while one is running and asserts the documented behavior (refuse, focus existing, or explicitly support multi-instance) occurs deterministically.

requirement: The pre-fader insert's 34-channel layout is fixed and documented: channels 1-2=strip1 L/R, 3-4=strip2, 5-6=strip3, 7-8=strip4, 9-10=strip5, 11-18=virtual input (8ch), 19-26=virtual AUX (8ch), 27-34=VIO3 (8ch), identical on the driver's input and output sides.
acceptance_test: Unit test asserts the insert channel-to-strip mapping function returns exactly the documented layout for all 34 indices, on both the insert-in and insert-out directions.

requirement: A modifier-assisted bulk-assign action sets 8 consecutive ASIO patch channels at once (e.g. auto-incrementing from a chosen starting channel), speeding up wiring an 8-channel ASIO interface to a strip/bus block.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test invokes the bulk-assign gesture starting at ASIO channel N and asserts 8 consecutive patch slots are set to channels N..N+7 in one action.

requirement: A Patch.composite[j] value of 0 means 'this composite channel uses the bus's own channel j' (pass-through), while a non-zero value selects a specific input channel by 1-based index.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets composite channel 3 to 0 and asserts it passes the bus's own channel 3 through; sets it to a specific input channel index and asserts that input is selected instead.

feature: Bus-assign changes do not disturb per-bus gain layers
spec_ref: PM p.9, p.67 (GainLayer independent of A/B assign)
requirement: Toggling a strip's bus-assign button for bus X does not reset or alter that strip's already-stored GainLayer[X] value; re-enabling routing to a bus restores its previously configured sub-mix level.
acceptance_test: Unit test sets a non-default GainLayer for bus X, disables then re-enables the strip's assignment to bus X, and asserts GainLayer[X] is unchanged throughout.

requirement: Assigning an ASIO output channel index beyond the connected ASIO device's actual channel count is rejected (or clamped with a diagnostic) rather than silently wrapping or crashing.
acceptance_test: Integration test patches a bus to an ASIO channel index beyond a mock device's reported channel count and asserts a documented rejection/diagnostic occurs, with no engine crash or silent wraparound.

feature: ASIO bus/strip patch requires ASIO-on-A1 precondition
requirement: The ASIO input/output channel-patch UI and API calls are only meaningful (and only take effect) when bus A1 currently has an ASIO device selected; attempting to use them otherwise is a documented no-op with a clear status, not a silent failure.
acceptance_test: Integration test issues patch.asio/patch.OutAx calls while A1 has a non-ASIO device selected and asserts a clear 'ASIO not active on A1' status is reported rather than a silent no-op.

feature: Insert return replaces rather than mixes with strip input
spec_ref: PM p.93; vendor user guide quoted in reference doc
requirement: When a strip's pre-fader insert is active and returning audio, that returned signal fully replaces the strip's own device/NetAudio input for downstream processing rather than being additively mixed with it.
acceptance_test: Integration test feeds both a live strip input and an insert-return signal simultaneously and asserts only the insert-return signal proceeds downstream once the insert is active for that channel.

feature: Recorder routing is independent of the main strip/bus assign matrix
requirement: Arming a strip or bus for recording (Recorder.ArmStrip/ArmBus) does not require or imply any change to that strip's/bus's normal A1-A5/B1-B3 routing assignments, and a bus can be armed for recording while carrying no output device at all.
acceptance_test: Integration test arms a bus that has zero routing assignments and no device, feeds it via Composite, and asserts the recorder still captures its content while the bus produces no other output.

feature: Routing-matrix state observable via RT snapshot
spec_ref: N spec RT-packet 0 bus/strip routing bits
requirement: The current strip-to-bus routing matrix is included in the real-time telemetry snapshot (per-strip/per-bus routing bitfields) so a remote UI can render the full matrix without polling every individual assign parameter.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets a known routing pattern and asserts the RT-packet-0 equivalent snapshot's routing bitfields decode to exactly that pattern.

feature: Physical-strip ASIO-patch channel count matches 2-per-strip model
requirement: The ASIO input patch exposes exactly 2 channel slots per physical strip (10 total for 5 strips), consistent with the fixed 2-channel-per-hardware-strip model elsewhere in the engine.
acceptance_test: Unit test asserts the ASIO input patch parameter space has exactly 10 addressable slots, 2 per physical strip in strip order.

feature: Composite Patch is one global table shared by all Composite-mode buses
requirement: There is exactly one Composite Patch table; any bus set to Composite mode outputs that same shared 8-channel patch, so two Composite buses always carry identical content (by design, for multi-destination recording/DAW use).
acceptance_test: Integration test sets two different buses to Composite mode and asserts both output the identical shared composite signal; changing the shared patch affects both simultaneously.

requirement: Settings, presets, and recordings default to platform-idiomatic locations (e.g. XDG config/data dirs on Linux, Application Support on macOS, a documented folder under the user's profile on Windows) rather than a fixed hard-coded path.
acceptance_test: Integration test runs on each target OS and asserts the default settings/preset/recording paths resolve to the documented platform-idiomatic location.

requirement: A one-time import utility reads the incumbent's XML settings format (strip/bus parameters, routing, options) and converts it into the native settings format, easing migration for existing users.
acceptance_test: Integration test feeds a representative incumbent-format XML settings file to the importer and asserts the resulting native settings file reproduces every mapped parameter correctly.

feature: MIDI map stored and versioned independently of main settings
requirement: The MIDI mapping (bindings + feedback options) is saved/loaded as its own named file, independent of the main mixer-settings save/load cycle, so a MIDI map can be shared or swapped without affecting other settings.
acceptance_test: Integration test saves a MIDI map, changes it, loads a different saved map, and asserts only the MIDI bindings change while all other current settings remain untouched.

feature: NetAudio configuration included in main settings, excluded from presets
requirement: NetAudio stream configuration (names/IPs/ports/quality/routes) is saved and restored as part of the main settings file, but is explicitly excluded from the 64-slot preset bank, matching the documented preset-exclusion list.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures NetAudio streams, saves/reloads main settings and asserts they are restored; stores and recalls a preset and asserts NetAudio configuration is unaffected by the preset recall.

requirement: A periodic auto-save snapshot of current settings is kept so an unexpected process termination does not lose more than a documented, bounded amount of configuration work.
acceptance_test: Integration test makes a configuration change, simulates an unclean process termination before an explicit save, restarts, and asserts the auto-saved snapshot (not just the last explicit save) is offered/restored within the documented time bound.

feature: Settings file schema validated on load with actionable errors
spec_ref: PM p.110 ('Saved XML File Inconsistencies' defect)
requirement: Loading a settings file with a structurally invalid or out-of-range field produces a specific, actionable error identifying the offending field and does not silently apply a partially-corrupt configuration, fixing the incumbent's documented XML-corruption failure mode.
acceptance_test: Unit test loads a settings file with one deliberately corrupted field (missing value, out-of-range number) and asserts the loader reports the exact field/reason and does not apply the rest of the file as a half-valid state.

requirement: The control-API's parameter-name string parser (Strip[i].X / Bus[i].X / dotted family names) safely rejects malformed, oversized, or adversarially-crafted name strings without memory-safety violations.
acceptance_test: Fuzz test feeds the parameter-name parser a large corpus of malformed/oversized/adversarial strings and asserts no crash, panic, or memory-safety violation across an extended fuzzing budget, integrated into CI.

requirement: Installation requests elevated/administrator privileges only for the specific steps that require it (virtual-device driver registration), not for the entire installer process or ordinary application runtime.
acceptance_test: Manual test runs the installer under a monitoring tool and asserts elevation is requested only around the driver-registration step, and the application itself runs at standard user privilege thereafter.

feature: Cryptographically secure key material for sync transport
requirement: Encryption keys/session secrets for the optional sync transport are generated using a cryptographically secure random source and never derived from predictable inputs (hostname, timestamp, sequential counters).
acceptance_test: Unit test asserts the key-generation routine is backed by the platform's CSPRNG and that two independently generated keys/sessions never collide across a large sample and show no detectable pattern versus a statistical randomness test.

requirement: The encrypted sync transport includes a sequence number or nonce per packet that a receiver uses to reject a replayed (previously seen, re-sent) packet rather than reprocessing it.
acceptance_test: Integration test captures a valid encrypted sync-transport packet, re-sends (replays) it after time has passed, and asserts the receiver detects and discards the replay rather than reapplying its content.

feature: Local control-protocol IPC restricted to the invoking user
requirement: On multi-user operating systems, the local IPC channel between the UI process and the engine process is only connectable by processes running as the same OS user (or an explicitly authorized loopback client), not by other local accounts.
acceptance_test: Integration test attempts to connect to the engine's local control-protocol endpoint from a process running as a different OS user and asserts the connection is refused.

requirement: A single engine instance can run plain (VBAN-compatible) streams and encrypted sync-transport streams concurrently on different stream slots without interference, so a LAN-interop stream and a VPN multi-room stream can coexist.
acceptance_test: Integration test runs one plain-protocol stream to a legacy-compatible receiver and one sync-transport stream to an OPENMIX receiver at the same time and asserts both deliver correct audio with no cross-interference or shared-state corruption.

feature: Bandwidth-aware quality throttling on constrained links
spec_ref: N spec Network Quality levels; PM p.55 guidance
requirement: Both transports allow a per-stream bandwidth/quality ceiling suited to constrained Wi-Fi/VPN links (mirroring the plain protocol's Net Quality levels), so a user on a slow link can trade latency for reliability without manual packet-size tuning.
acceptance_test: Integration test runs a stream under a simulated low-bandwidth/high-jitter link at each quality tier and asserts higher tiers (Slow/Very Slow-equivalent) show measurably fewer drop/error events than lower tiers under identical simulated conditions.

requirement: When configuring an outgoing stream, the UI suggests the plain protocol for a same-subnet (LAN) destination and the encrypted sync transport for any destination reached through a non-local network path (VPN/WAN), without forcing the choice.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test enters a same-subnet destination and asserts the plain-protocol suggestion is shown; enters a routed/VPN destination and asserts the sync-transport suggestion is shown instead, with the user free to override either.

requirement: Uninstalling the virtual-device component leaves no orphaned/ghost devices in the OS device list on any of the three target platforms.
acceptance_test: Integration test installs then uninstalls the virtual-device component on each platform's CI runner and asserts the OS device enumeration shows zero remaining OPENMIX virtual devices afterward.

requirement: Virtual playback/recording endpoint names follow one consistent naming scheme (e.g. 'OPENMIX Input', 'OPENMIX Out B1') across Windows, macOS, and Linux, so cross-platform documentation and automation scripts do not need per-OS special-casing.
acceptance_test: Integration test enumerates virtual endpoints on each platform's backend and asserts the display names match the documented cross-platform naming pattern exactly.

feature: macOS driver notarization for HAL plug-in
spec_ref: Decision spine architecture #3 (signing parity with Windows)
requirement: The macOS HAL plug-in is signed and notarized per current Apple requirements so it installs and loads without Gatekeeper warnings on a clean macOS system.
acceptance_test: Manual release-checklist test installs the notarized HAL plug-in on a clean macOS VM with default Gatekeeper settings and asserts no security warning blocks installation or loading.

feature: Backend selection is a runtime/config choice, not a rebuild
requirement: Which host-I/O and virtual-device backend is active is selected via runtime configuration appropriate to the current OS, not via a compile-time-only switch, so a single distributed binary per OS works without per-backend rebuilds.
acceptance_test: Integration test on one platform build toggles between its available backends (e.g. WASAPI vs null, or PipeWire vs ALSA) via configuration alone and asserts both work without recompilation.

spec_ref: Vendor user guide quoted in reference doc ('DO NOT SELECT THE SAME AUDIO DEVICE TWICE')
requirement: The engine detects when the same physical device is about to be opened twice across different audio points (e.g. ASIO on A1 and WDM/MME on a strip input) and warns rather than silently producing the documented instability.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures the same mock physical device on two different audio points and asserts a clear warning/diagnostic is surfaced before or upon engine start.

requirement: Every virtual-strip ASIO device presents a fixed 8-in/8-out channel contract to connecting clients regardless of how many of those channels are actually carrying signal.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects a mock ASIO client and asserts it is offered exactly 8 input and 8 output channels, independent of upstream channel activity.

requirement: If a selected ASIO driver does not provide a native control panel (or it fails to launch), the UI surfaces a clear message instead of a silent no-op or crash.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test selects a mock ASIO driver configured to fail control-panel launch and asserts a clear, non-crashing error message is shown.

feature: Forced ASIO buffer size falls back on driver refusal
requirement: If a forced ASIO buffer size is refused by the driver, the engine falls back to the driver's own default/reported size and clearly reports the effective size actually in use, rather than failing to start.
acceptance_test: Integration test forces a buffer size a mock ASIO driver rejects and asserts the engine starts successfully at the driver's reported fallback size, with that size clearly exposed via the control API.

spec_ref: PM p.94 note ('new control: PAN and BUS Assignations')
requirement: In addition to gain/mute/solo/etc., pan-panel positions and per-strip bus-assign buttons are individually MIDI-mappable controls.
acceptance_test: Unit test binds a MIDI CC to a strip's pan position and a MIDI note to a bus-assign button, then asserts each responds correctly to its bound MIDI input.

requirement: Messages from the primary and the secondary 'MIDI Extra' input device are merged into one logical input stream for mapping/learn purposes, so either device can drive any mapped control.
acceptance_test: Integration test sends the same mapped MIDI message from each of the two configured input devices independently and asserts both trigger the mapped control identically.

spec_ref: Decision spine (robustness; not explicitly documented upstream but a standard MIDI-app safety norm)
requirement: A panic action sends an all-notes-off / reset-controllers message set to the configured MIDI output device(s), for recovering from a stuck-note or runaway-feedback condition.
acceptance_test: Unit test triggers the panic action and asserts the documented all-notes-off/reset-controllers MIDI message sequence is sent to every configured MIDI output.
notes: Not explicitly documented in the source reference; included as a standard robustness feature consistent with the decision spine's defect-fix intent.

spec_ref: Decision spine (auto-reconnect defect-fix, applied to MIDI)
requirement: If a mapped MIDI input or output device is unplugged and later reconnected, the mapping engine automatically resumes using it without requiring the user to re-select the device.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates unplug/replug of a mock MIDI device that is currently mapped and asserts mapped controls resume responding to/sending MIDI without manual re-selection.

requirement: A dedicated configuration surface (equivalent to the incumbent's VIO Control Panel) lets a user test and set each virtual endpoint's internal latency value, with elevated privileges required only for the specific change that needs them.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test opens the latency configuration surface for one virtual endpoint, sets a new latency value, and asserts the change takes effect on both the endpoint and its paired output as documented.

feature: Insert-active indicator reflects live connection state
requirement: A per-strip insert-active indicator (equivalent to the incumbent's 'i' icon) is true exactly when an external client is currently connected to and returning audio on that strip's insert channels, and reflects a disconnect immediately.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects then disconnects a mock insert client on one strip's channels and asserts the indicator turns on immediately upon connection and off immediately upon disconnection.

feature: Virtual ASIO multi-client mix order independence
requirement: When multiple clients are connected to the same virtual strip's ASIO device, their combined output is summed into that strip's input regardless of the order in which the clients connected.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects 3 mock ASIO clients to one virtual strip's ASIO device in different orders across repeated runs and asserts the resulting summed signal is identical (order-independent) in every run.

spec_ref: PM 'At a glance' numbers table (LEARN ~10s and BYPASS since 3.1.1.9)
requirement: A LEARN action captures roughly 10 seconds of the strip's current noise floor to calibrate the denoiser's noise profile, after which denoising is applied relative to the learned profile.
acceptance_test: Integration test feeds a known noise-plus-signal test file, triggers LEARN during a 10-second noise-only segment, then plays the signal segment and asserts noise-floor reduction is measurably improved versus the un-calibrated default profile.

requirement: A documented gesture (right-click equivalent) cycles a hardware strip's single 2D-panel display among the Color, 3D Position, and Modulation panels without changing any underlying parameter values.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test performs the cycling gesture 3 times on a strip and asserts the displayed panel cycles Color -> 3D -> Modulation -> Color, with no change to the Color_x/y, Pan_x/y, or fx_x/y parameter values during cycling.

requirement: A documented gesture toggles a hardware strip between its simple knob view and a detailed compressor/gate parameter view (transfer graph, gain-reduction meters) in place of the strip's pan panel.
acceptance_test: E2E UI test performs the toggle gesture and asserts the detail view (transfer graph + meters) replaces the pan panel, and repeating the gesture restores the pan panel.

feature: Bandwidth budget matches documented per-stream table
spec_ref: N spec Bandwidth section (computed kbps table)
requirement: For each combination of sample rate, channel count, and bit depth in the documented reference table, the actual on-wire bandwidth (including per-packet header/UDP/IP overhead) stays within a small, documented tolerance of the computed reference figure.
acceptance_test: Perf test streams each documented (SR, channels, bit-depth) combination and measures actual on-wire bytes/sec, asserting it matches the computed reference bandwidth within the documented tolerance.

requirement: On a wired LAN, the transport layer itself (excluding buffering/jitter strategy) contributes well under 1 ms of one-way latency at typical LAN distances, consistent with the documented wire-transport figures.
acceptance_test: Perf test measures raw one-way wire transport time on a wired LAN loopback/two-host setup at minimal buffering and asserts it is within the documented sub-millisecond order of magnitude.

feature: Insert-conflict validation when recording pre-fader inputs
spec_ref: Reference doc §19 (forum note: insert must be disabled to record cleanly)
requirement: Arming a strip for pre-fader recording while that strip's insert point is actively returning external audio surfaces a clear validation notice (since pre-fader recording and an active insert return interact), rather than silently recording an unexpected signal.
acceptance_test: Integration test arms a strip for recording while its insert is actively connected and returning audio, and asserts a clear notice is surfaced identifying the interaction before/while recording.

feature: Macro app NetAudio configuration (MIDI/TEXT/FRAME stream counts)
spec_ref: PM p.84-85 (Dec 2025: 2 MIDI out, 4 TEXT out, 1 FRAME out, 1 TEXT in)
requirement: The macro/automation application independently configures 2 outgoing NetAudio-MIDI streams, 4 outgoing NetAudio-TEXT streams, 1 outgoing NetAudio-FRAME stream (for sharing the macro view), and 1 incoming NetAudio-TEXT stream (for remote mouse control), separate from the main engine's NetAudio configuration.
acceptance_test: Integration test configures all 8 of the macro app's NetAudio stream slots to distinct destinations and asserts each transmits/receives independently without cross-talk, and independently of the main engine's own NetAudio stream configuration.

feature: Macro app version-compatibility check against engine
requirement: The macro/automation application checks that the connected engine meets its documented minimum compatible version and surfaces a clear incompatibility notice rather than silently misbehaving against an older/newer engine.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects the macro app to a mock engine reporting a version below the documented minimum and asserts a clear incompatibility notice is shown rather than allowing silent operation.
