spec_ref: Decision spine (developer-experience improvement over incumbent's static PDF)
requirement: The control API exposes a machine-readable introspection call that lists every available parameter family, its index ranges, value ranges, and data type, so client tooling can be generated/validated automatically instead of relying on a static document.
acceptance_test: Unit test calls the introspection endpoint and asserts every parameter family documented in this test matrix's control-api/dsp-strip/dsp-bus/etc. rows appears with a matching range/type description.

feature: OSC transport for the canonical control protocol
requirement: The same canonical parameter grammar is reachable over OSC in addition to JSON/WebSocket, per the decision spine's 'one canonical JSON/WebSocket + OSC control protocol' requirement.
acceptance_test: Integration test sends an OSC message addressing a documented parameter (e.g. /strip/0/gain) and asserts the identical effect as the equivalent JSON/WebSocket call, and that a subscribed OSC client receives change notifications too.

feature: JSON/WebSocket transport for the canonical control protocol
requirement: The canonical control protocol is reachable over a JSON-messages-over-WebSocket transport, supporting get, set, batch-script, subscribe, and level-query operations equivalent to the compatibility shim's C-ABI surface.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects over WebSocket, performs get/set/batch/subscribe/level-query operations, and asserts behavior matches the equivalent compatibility-shim C-ABI calls exercised in the shim's own test row.

feature: Reverb preset recall matches documented parameter sets
requirement: Recalling any of the documented reverb room-type or style presets sets every underlying reverb parameter (room type/size, dry/wet, pre-delay, early-reflection amount, decay factor, EQ) to that preset's exact stored values.
acceptance_test: Unit test recalls each documented preset and asserts every underlying parameter matches the stored preset table exactly, with no residual value carried over from the previously active preset.

requirement: Each of the 8 delay taps has an independent On (include in mix) and Solo (isolate this tap only) control.
acceptance_test: Unit test toggles On for a subset of taps and asserts only those contribute to the output; enables Solo on one tap and asserts only that tap's echo is audible regardless of other taps' On state.

spec_ref: Decision spine (quality bar, not explicit in source)
requirement: Switching a bus's mode at runtime (e.g. Normal to Composite) does not produce a click/pop exceeding a documented amplitude/duration threshold, even though the channel-mapping formula changes discontinuously.
acceptance_test: Golden test switches bus mode mid-stream on a continuous test tone and asserts any transient at the switch point stays within the documented click-amplitude/duration budget.

feature: Bus EQ and strip EQ share one validated filter engine
spec_ref: PM p.25 ('exactly the same EQ than on Master BUS')
requirement: The 6-cell parametric filter engine used for bus EQ and hardware-strip EQ is a single shared, independently-tested DSP component (not duplicated/diverging implementations), differing only in channel count (8 vs 2) and UI presentation.
acceptance_test: Property test runs the identical filter-type/frequency/gain/Q matrix through both the bus-EQ code path and the strip-EQ code path and asserts bit-identical (or tolerance-identical) per-channel output, confirming a shared implementation.

feature: Device hot-list refresh without engine restart
spec_ref: Decision spine (defect-fix: reduce manual restart dependence)
requirement: The device selector's available-device list refreshes automatically when the OS reports a device added/removed event, without requiring a manual 'rescan' or full engine restart to see the change.
acceptance_test: Integration test adds and removes a mock device on the null backend's device-notification hook and asserts the device selector's live list updates automatically within a documented short delay, with no engine restart.

feature: Sample-rate/bit-depth mismatch is corrected, not silently distorted
requirement: Whenever a device is opened at a sample rate or bit depth different from what the engine expects at that point, the engine performs correct conversion rather than reinterpreting/truncating samples incorrectly (which would otherwise produce pitch-shifted or noisy audio).
acceptance_test: Golden test opens a mock device at a mismatched rate/bit-depth and asserts the resulting audio, after the engine's conversion stage, is pitch- and duration-correct against a reference signal.

feature: Engine restart preserves full parameter state
spec_ref: PM p.43 (Restart Audio Engine 'sends no remoting data' but keeps config)
requirement: A full engine restart (device re-open cycle) preserves every currently-configured strip/bus/fx/patch/option/recorder parameter exactly as it was before the restart; only the audio streams themselves are re-opened.
acceptance_test: Integration test sets a non-trivial full parameter state, triggers a restart, and asserts every parameter reads back identically once the engine resumes streaming.

feature: Deterministic startup order for dependent subsystems
requirement: Engine subsystems start in a deterministic, dependency-respecting order (state store, DSP graph, host-I/O backends, control-API listeners, NetAudio service) so a client connecting immediately at startup never observes a partially-initialized state.
acceptance_test: Integration test connects a control-API client at the earliest possible moment after process launch and asserts it never observes an inconsistent/partial state (e.g. a parameter family present without its default values fully set).

feature: RTSP/RTP audio ingest from IP cameras
requirement: An input source can pull the audio track from an RTSP/RTP stream (as published by a typical IP camera) and feed it into a virtual input strip, closing the gap where the incumbent has no RTSP/RTP/HTTP/HLS/Icecast ingest at all.
acceptance_test: Integration test points the ingest source at a local RTSP test server (e.g. a MediaMTX/go2rtc fixture) publishing a known tone, and asserts the tone arrives on the target strip within a documented latency bound and without format errors.

feature: Two-way IP-camera audio: backchannel to camera speaker
requirement: A bus can be sent out over an ONVIF/RTSP backchannel to an IP camera's built-in speaker, so the operator can talk back through the camera, matching the recipe described for IP-camera two-way audio.
acceptance_test: Integration test sends a known tone from a bus to a backchannel-capable RTSP test fixture and asserts the fixture receives the tone with correct channel count and no more than one documented format conversion in the path.

feature: HLS/Icecast internet-radio ingest as an input source
requirement: An input source can decode an HLS or Icecast/SHOUTcast stream URL and feed the decoded audio into a virtual input strip, another gap the incumbent does not cover.
acceptance_test: Integration test points the ingest source at a local HLS/Icecast test server serving a known tone and asserts continuous, gapless playback on the target strip for a multi-segment/multi-minute run.

feature: Automatic reconnect for dropped IP-camera/HLS/Icecast sources
spec_ref: mixboard.txt Part 3 IP-streams chapter #6; defect-fix auto-reconnect (Decision spine #7)
requirement: When an RTSP, HLS or Icecast ingest source disconnects (camera reboot, network blip, server restart), the engine retries with backoff and resumes feeding the same strip once the source returns, without operator intervention, extending the auto-reconnect defect fix to network ingest sources.
acceptance_test: Integration test kills and restarts the fixture server mid-stream and asserts the strip silently mutes, retries on a documented backoff schedule, and resumes audio within a documented bound after the server returns, with the event logged.

requirement: A new receiver can join, or an existing receiver can leave, a running multi-room stream group at any time without stopping or reconfiguring the stream for the receivers already in the group, extending the static multi-room grouping model (T-network-ext-005) with runtime membership changes.
acceptance_test: Integration test starts a group of two receivers, adds a third receiver mid-session and asserts it reaches sync-transport alignment within the documented tolerance without audible interruption on the first two, then removes one receiver and asserts the remaining two are unaffected.

feature: Sync/plain transport operation over a routed VPN tunnel
spec_ref: mixboard.txt Part 3 IP-streams chapter #4; Decision spine architecture #5
requirement: Both the plain VBAN-compatible mode and the optional sync transport work over a routed point-to-point VPN link (e.g. WireGuard) where broadcast-based discovery does not reach, by supporting explicit unicast endpoint configuration end to end, matching the incumbent's documented VPN recipe.
acceptance_test: Interop test tunnels a stream between two hosts over a WireGuard test link with broadcast discovery disabled, using only explicit IP:port configuration, and asserts audio transfers correctly in both plain and sync-transport modes.

feature: Non-Windows/headless endpoint joins a multi-room group via the control protocol
requirement: A non-Windows or headless client (e.g. a Linux single-board receiver) can join a multi-room sync-transport group and be controlled (volume, mute, group membership) purely over the canonical control protocol, with no engine-native GUI required on that endpoint.
acceptance_test: Integration test runs the engine's control-protocol client library on a Linux fixture, joins a group, and asserts group membership, sync alignment and volume/mute commands all take effect as they would from the primary UI.

feature: Bluetooth output endpoint with disclosed latency and auto-reconnect
requirement: A bus can be routed to a Bluetooth A2DP output device; the UI discloses the extra latency this endpoint adds rather than hiding it, and the endpoint automatically reconnects and resumes routing after a Bluetooth radio drop, without requiring the user to reselect the device.
acceptance_test: Integration test routes a bus to a Bluetooth-sink test fixture, measures and asserts the reported latency figure is within a documented margin of the actual measured round trip, then simulates a radio drop and asserts automatic reconnection and resumed audio within a documented bound.

requirement: An input strip fed by a 2.4 GHz proprietary USB wireless dongle or wireless-mic receiver is automatically delay- and clock-compensated against the engine's main clock, so it stays sample-aligned with wired strips despite the dongle's independent, asynchronous clock.
acceptance_test: Integration test feeds a known transient through a simulated asynchronous 2.4 GHz dongle input alongside the same transient on a wired strip, and asserts the two remain aligned within a documented sample tolerance over a multi-minute run with no accumulating drift.

feature: Wi-Fi roaming handoff for NetAudio clients
requirement: A NetAudio/sync-transport client that roams between access points on the same SSID keeps its session alive across the handoff, reconnecting automatically within a documented bound and logging the event, rather than silently dropping and requiring a manual re-pair.
acceptance_test: Integration test simulates an AP handoff (interface re-association) mid-stream on a client fixture and asserts the session resumes within a documented time bound with the handoff recorded in the diagnostic log, and no manual action required.

feature: Long-session clock-drift reconciliation for network endpoints
requirement: A network endpoint whose local sample clock drifts from the sender's over a long session (different device crystal, not just an SR-table mismatch) is continuously tracked and resampled to prevent accumulating clicks or dropouts, distinct from the engine's one-time per-stream SRC.
acceptance_test: Property/soak test runs a simulated sender/receiver pair with an injected small constant clock-rate offset for a multi-hour equivalent duration (accelerated in test time) and asserts no click/dropout events are recorded and drift stays bounded throughout.

requirement: When Wi-Fi NetAudio traffic and 2.4 GHz proprietary dongles/DECT devices share the band, the engine surfaces a diagnostic indicator (packet-loss/retry rate trending up) and suggests a channel or transport change, rather than leaving the operator to guess at glitches, matching the quick decision rules in the reference.
acceptance_test: Integration test injects a rising synthetic packet-loss/retry rate on a NetAudio link and asserts the diagnostic surfaces the condition and the suggested-action message once a documented threshold is crossed, and clears once the rate falls back below it.
